page.title: LAND OF OZ
page.content:
## Infobox

- Name: Land of Oz
- Place type: Country
- Status: Unreachable by ordinary means

## Biography

The Land of Oz is a country lying beyond the Deadly Sands, a barrier desert that "will Turn Any Living Flesh to Dust in an Instant." A sign at the edge of the sands names it "the LAND OF OZ" and states that "no one can Reach that Beautiful Country because of these Destroying Sands." Dorothy confirms the danger of the sands from her own experience, saying "it's true no one can live who tries to walk upon the sands." The Land of Oz encompasses the Emerald City, which Dorothy identifies as a place where she has friends who "would take care of them and send them safe home again."

## Appearance

No description of the land's interior is given beyond the sign calling it a "Beautiful Country." What is confirmed is the nature of its border: the surrounding sands turn any living flesh that touches them into dust, making the country's edge a lethal barrier rather than an ordinary frontier.

## Events

Dorothy, the shaggy man, Button-Bright, Toto, and Polychrome find themselves stranded at the edge of the Deadly Desert, unable to find a way across the sands to reach the Land of Oz.

## Trivia

- Dorothy states she has crossed the desert to the Land of Oz "more than once" before this occasion.
- The shaggy man brings in Johnny Dooit specifically to help the group find a way to cross the sands into the Land of Oz.

## References

<references/>

page.title: Land of Oz
page.content:
## Infobox

- Name: Land of Oz
- Notable landmark: the Water of Oblivion

## Biography

The Land of Oz is described as always beautiful, wherever one might go, even in its stranger, unfamiliar reaches where no houses or farmers can be found to guide travelers. It is home to unusual peoples, among them Fuddlecumjig and the Fuddles, said to be the most peculiar people in all the Land of Oz. Unlike the wider world, where people sail upon oceans for weeks without sighting land, there is no such thing as an ocean anywhere in the Land of Oz.

## Events

During their travels, Dorothy and the Wizard discuss airships, and the Wizard reveals he is working on a magic recipe meant to keep airships from ever reaching the Land of Oz. Elsewhere, the First and Foremost of the Phanfasms calls to conquer the Land of Oz, marshaling his Phanfasms in battle array and marching them into a tunnel toward the Emerald City. The Nome King's forces are ultimately turned back: General Guph is ordered to follow his master, the Nome King, and the Nomes quit the Land of Oz forever. The Phanfasms, Whimsies, and Growleywogs remain behind for a time, filling the gardens in such numbers that they trample the flowers and grass underfoot.

## Appearance

Among the notable features of the Land of Oz is a spring whose water seems clear and sparkling, bubbling up in a golden basin. Despite this inviting appearance, Ozma gravely declares it the most dangerous thing in all the Land of Oz, naming it the Water of Oblivion. Beyond such landmarks, travelers moving through unfamiliar parts of the country find no paths, houses, or farmers to guide them, even while the land itself remains beautiful throughout.

## Trivia

- No ocean exists anywhere in the Land of Oz, unlike the wider world beyond it.
- The Fuddlecumjig and the Fuddles are said to be the most peculiar people in all the Land of Oz.
- The spring known as the Water of Oblivion is described as the most dangerous thing in the entire Land of Oz.

## References

<references/>

page.title: Throne Room
page.content:
## Infobox

- Name: Throne Room
- Place type: Audience chamber

## Biography

The Throne Room is the chamber where Oz receives those who seek audience with him. Ladies and gentlemen of the court gather each morning in a great hall outside it, though they are never permitted to see Oz themselves. Access is tightly controlled: visitors are summoned at precise times and must knock and wait to be called in. When the Lion first entered, he found before the throne a Ball of Fire, so fierce and glowing he could scarcely bear to look at it; on another occasion, those who entered found no one in the room at all. Oz himself later admitted it was a great mistake ever letting his visitors into the Throne Room, since he otherwise refuses to see even his own subjects so that they continue to believe him something terrible.

## Events

In the Throne Room, Oz's disembodied Voice questions the visitors about the death of a witch and asks for another day to consider their request. Later, the four companions gather there again: the Scarecrow, the Tin Woodman, and the Lion each express contentment with what they received from Oz, while Dorothy alone insists she still wants to return to Aunt Em and Uncle Henry in Kansas.

## Biography

Quelala is a young man raised in the ruby palace of Gayelette, who used her magic to shape him into someone strong, good, and lovely, intending to take him as her husband. By the time he reached manhood, he was said to be the wisest and best man in the land, admired for his great beauty. Shortly before his wedding to Gayelette, he was walking beside a river dressed in a costume of pink silk and purple velvet when the King of the Winged Monkeys and his band seized him as a prank, carried him over the water, and dropped him in, mockingly asking whether the water had spotted his clothes.

page.content:
## Infobox

- Name: Palace
- Place type: Royal residence
- Region: Emerald City

## Biography

The Palace stands in the Emerald City and serves as the residence of Oz. Guest chambers reached through seven passages and up three flights of stairs hold beds with sheets of green silk and a green velvet counterpane. The Palace keeps a stock of silk on hand, later used to build a balloon, and its back yard houses a green cock and a hen. Oz himself remains largely confined to a set of rooms within the Palace, avoiding the outside world so his people will not discover he is not truly a Wizard.

## Events

The Guardian of the Gates leads visitors through the city streets to the Palace, where a soldier tells them Oz will see each of them alone, one per day. A balloon is later carried out in front of the Palace, drawing a crowd who watch it filled with hot air over a fire. Seen from a distance, the Palace's dome remains visible among the towers of the Emerald City.

page.title: Wizard
page.content:
## Biography

Known as Oz the Terrible, and hailed by the people of the Emerald City as the Wonderful Wizard, the Wizard is the ruler whom Dorothy travels to see in hopes of returning home. He does not like to have people ask to see him, and at first reacts angrily to her request, saying she should be sent back where she came from, before eventually consenting to grant her an audience. He later departs the Emerald City by balloon, calling for Dorothy to hurry aboard before it flies away; once airborne he finds he cannot bring the balloon back down, bids everyone farewell, and rises out of sight. Afterward the people remember him lovingly, saying to one another that Oz was always their friend.

## Relationships

**[[Dorothy]]** — wary alliance. Their interactions suggest a cautious, uneasy cooperation rather than open friendship.

**[[Scarecrow]]** — employment. Their bond seems to reflect a working tie connected to the Wizard's former rule over the Emerald City.

**[[Tin Woodman]]** — employment. Their connection appears to be one of service, though not explicitly detailed.

**[[Cowardly Lion]]** — employment. Their tie likewise suggests a bond of service rather than personal closeness.

**[[Guardian of the Gates]]** — employment. Their link seems to place the Guardian in the Wizard's service.

page.title: Wizard of Oz
page.content:
## Biography

The Wizard of Oz, known simply as the Wizard or the Wonderful Wizard, built the Emerald City, a city rendered entirely in shades of green according to Tip's account. He once ruled the Emerald City as its King, having taken the crown from Pastoria, the city's former King, before passing it on to the Scarecrow when he departed. When Dorothy came to the Emerald City with the Scarecrow and the Tin Woodman to ask him to send her back to Kansas, the Wizard could not do so, since he was not so much of a Wizard as he might have been. He is nonetheless credited with placing a heart of his own construction into the breast of the Tin Woodman, an act commemorated by a large painting hanging in the Tin Woodman's palace. During his reign the Soldier with the Green Whiskers served as his Royal Army, and people feared him enough that the army carried real weight. He later escaped the Emerald City in a balloon.

According to Glinda's investigation into his conduct, the Wizard's recorded actions included eating beans with a knife, paying three secret visits to old Mombi, and walking with a slight limp on his left foot; the Tin Woodman suggested, without certainty, that he might have originally come from a country called Omaha. Glinda's inquiry further concluded that the Wizard had taught Mombi some of his tricks of magic, which she took as evidence that Mombi had helped him conceal the infant Ozma, the rightful heir to the Emerald City's throne. Mombi herself, compelled by Glinda's truth-detecting pearl, confirmed that the Wizard brought her the infant Ozma and asked her to hide the child — Ozma being, by Mombi's account, the daughter of the King whose throne the Wizard had taken.

## Relationships

**[[Nick Chopper]]** — the bond seems to have soured over time; though the Wizard is credited with fashioning Nick Chopper's tin heart, the record suggests Nick Chopper grew angry enough to threaten exposing him, hinting at an adversarial turn.

**[[Old Mombi]]** — the two appear to share a guarded arrangement rather than open friendship; Glinda's inquiry suggests the Wizard taught Mombi several of his tricks of magic, implying she aided him in return, likely in concealing the infant Ozma.

**[[The Scarecrow]]** — like Nick Chopper, the Scarecrow reportedly grew angry at the Wizard and threatened to expose him, suggesting a falling-out despite the Wizard having passed the crown of the Emerald City on to him.

**[[Tip]]** — the connection is inferential; Tip recounts the Wizard's failed attempt to send Dorothy back to Kansas, a narration whose tone could hint at some skepticism toward the Wizard, though no direct confrontation between them is described.

**[[Dorothy]]** — she once sought out the Wizard to ask him to send her back to Kansas, only for him to fail her; this unmet request could suggest a strained relationship, though the excerpts describe no open conflict between them.

page.title: WIZARD

infobox_fields.alias: Mr. Wizard, THE WIZARD, The Wizard, Wizard

page.content:
## Biography

The Wizard, also known as Mr. Wizard, is introduced as "the same humbug Wizard as before," a description recalling that he had once "mounted into the sky in a balloon" and that others had been waiting for him to come down again.

During the crossing of the Valley of Voe, the Wizard rubbed a leaf of a strange plant upon the soles of Dorothy's shoes and upon his own, allowing them to walk upon the water without sinking. He then drew the buggy down the bank and out onto the broad river while Dorothy remained seated in it with Eureka in her arms, and once the buggy reached the middle of the stream he returned to the bank to assist Zeb and Jim in crossing as well.

In the glass city, when it was revealed that a door thought closed had allowed Dorothy's white kitten to slip out and run up the stairs, the Wizard exchanged startled glances with Dorothy, both recalling how often Eureka had longed to eat a piglet.

The Wizard was later named among the nine members of a jury assembled by Ozma, seated alongside the Cowardly Lion, the Hungry Tiger, Jim the Cab-horse, the Yellow Hen, the Scarecrow, Tik-tok the Machine Man, the Sawhorse, and Zeb of Hugson's Ranch, in a body Ozma described as mixing animals and people so that all her subjects could be admitted to hear the testimony.

## Narrative role

The Wizard, also known as Mr. Wizard or The Wizard, first proves his mettle underground in the Land of the Mangaboos by defeating the thorny Sorcerer Gwig in a contest of magic, an encounter through which he also learns that the Mangaboos grow from bushes rather than being born. Building on this success, he and Dorothy pick the ripe Royal Princess from the Royal Bush, and she promptly deposes the Prince to take the throne as the Mangaboos' new ruler. The new Princess spares the Wizard along with Dorothy and Zeb, but condemns Jim, Eureka, and the piglets to be driven into the Black Pit within the mountain. Facing exile from the glass city, the Wizard, Dorothy, and Zeb resist eating the invisibility-granting dama-fruit and instead learn they must press on toward Pyramid Mountain, receiving along the way an offer of help from an unseen ally confronting the threat of bears. That help proves decisive in the Valley of Voe, where the Wizard, Dorothy, Zeb, Jim, and Eureka escape invisible bears by rubbing magic leaves on their feet to walk across water. Later, the Wizard quietly gives the Tin Woodman a duplicate piglet, meant to serve as proof of Eureka's innocence should she be convicted.

## Personality

The Wizard proves decisive and quick-witted under pressure: warned by an unseen voice of danger in the Valley, he acts "without hesitation," steering the buggy to safety across the river before doubling back to assist Zeb and Jim — securing his own charge first, then returning for the others. His gratitude is expressed openly, as when he cries out "joyfully" upon being helped.

He is also observant and quietly complicit rather than confrontational: when the Princess asks whether a door had been left open, the Wizard and Dorothy "exchange startled glances," both recalling Eureka's known taste for piglets without voicing the suspicion aloud. Beyond his own actions, he is described by the narration as "the same humbug Wizard as before," marking him as a figure whose wonders are regarded as trickery rather than true sorcery.

## Appearance

A formal portrait of the Wizard, displayed during the trial proceedings in the Emerald City, stands as the only depiction referenced within his story.

## Powers

The Wizard is not shown to possess genuine magical power; the record calls him "the same humbug Wizard as before," pointing to a reputation for magic that exceeds his real abilities. What he does demonstrate is practical resourcefulness: when danger threatens his companions, he applies the leaves of a plant whose virtues keep the buggy and its passengers from sinking, rubbing a leaf on Dorothy's shoes and his own before driving the buggy down the bank and out onto the river, then returning to help Zeb and Jim cross safely.

## Relationships

**[[DOROTHY]]** — friend. Their bond seems close: the Wizard tells her "I remember you very well," suggesting a familiarity built up over their shared journey.

**[[Zeb]]** — ally. The two seem allied through the ordeals they face together; the Wizard's question "But why destroy my friends?" could indicate a protective concern toward companions such as Zeb.

**[[Jim]]** — ally. Jim and the Wizard travel side by side in the buggy, as suggested by the remark "It's violet, said the Wizard, who was in the buggy," which points to their continued proximity during the journey.

**[[Prince]]** — acquaintance. Their contact appears limited to an exchange in which the Prince questions the Wizard, "why are you here, in the Land of the Mangaboos?", suggesting only a passing, formal acquaintance.

**[[Eureka]]** — acquaintance. The bond seems slight, hinted at when the Wizard tells his companions, Eureka among them, "I don't mind telling you, who are my friends, that the thing was only a trick," suggesting a shared, if minor, camaraderie.

## Trivia

- Long before falling into the underground lands of the Mangaboos, the Wizard was known for having once ascended into the sky in a balloon, an event children had heard about and for which they awaited his return.
- He is described as "the same humbug Wizard as before," implying a reputation for trickery that predates the present events.
- On the jury Ozma assembled to hear testimony, the Wizard was the sole human name among otherwise non-human members: the Cowardly Lion, the Hungry Tiger, Jim the Cab-horse, the Yellow Hen, the Scarecrow, Tik-tok the Machine Man, the Sawhorse, and Zeb of Hugson's Ranch.

page.content:
## Biography

Le Wizard, aussi désigné sous les formes « THE WIZARD » et « The Wizard », réside dans l'Emerald City, située au centre d'Oz, à l'endroit où se rencontrent les quatre pays qui composent ce territoire.

Il est présenté comme celui qui a donné à Nick Chopper — l'homme de fer-blanc — un cœur qualifié de « merveilleux » dans ce contexte, ce qui souligne son rôle de figure capable d'accomplir des actes hors du commun.

Dans un échange rapporté autour du Love Magnet, le Wizard affirme que tout le monde aime déjà Dorothy, une remarque qui laisse entrevoir une opinion favorable envers elle, sans que davantage de détails ne soient donnés sur la nature exacte de leur lien.

## Narrative role

The Wizard appears at [[Ozma]]'s birthday celebration, which draws many guests to the palace and its grounds. Afterward, he sends several of the visitors home inside magic bubbles, while Dorothy returns to Kansas by the Magic Belt.

## Personality

The Wizard shows a practical, fair-minded streak: when the shaggy man offers to give the Love Magnet to Dorothy, the Wizard points out that "every one loves Dorothy already," and redirects the gift to Button-Bright instead. This reaction suggests he reasons about what people already possess rather than letting a gift go to someone who does not need it, and reveals him as attentive to the social standing of those around him.

## Powers

The Wizard is credited with giving Nick Chopper a heart, the enchanted organ Nick Chopper carries as the Tin Man.

## Relationships

**[[Dorothy]]** — friend. The Wizard seems to hold Dorothy in particular esteem, noting that "every one loves Dorothy already," and greeted her with much affection.

**[[Nick Chopper]]** — other. The Wizard appears to have given Nick Chopper "a lovely heart," suggesting some past act of aid on Nick Chopper's behalf.

**[[Button-Bright]]** — acquaintance. Button-Bright seems to have shown no fear of the Wizard, counted among those "not at all afraid of the wonderful personage."

**[[Ozma]]** — employment. Ozma appears to have called on the Wizard's services, asking him "to give them an exhibition of his magic."

**[[Polly]]** — acquaintance. Like Button-Bright, Polly seems to have shown no fear of the Wizard, counted among those "not at all afraid of the wonderful personage."

## Trivia

- The Wizard gave Nick Chopper, the Tin Woodman, the heart he now has.
- When the shaggy man offered to give up the Love Magnet to Dorothy, the Wizard remarked that "every one loves Dorothy already," prompting the shaggy man to give it to Button-Bright instead.

## Biography

The Wizard travels with Dorothy's party through regions of the Land of Oz he admits he has never visited before. He shows familiarity with local lore, describing the Fuddlecumjig and the Fuddles as "the most peculiar people in all the Land of Oz" and questioning a kangaroo about their temperament. His sense of direction helps the group identify Flutterbudget Center along the road. He speaks with dry wit, as when he answers a woman's fear of losing a foot by noting she might have lost her head instead, and he shows concern for strangers, stopping a visibly nervous man to ask if something is wrong. At the Emperor's castle, the Wizard explains that Winkies keep the structure polished and that the Emperor once had himself nickel-plated, calling him "the brightest man in all the world... and the kindest-hearted."

page.content:
## Biography

Gayelette is a sorceress who lives in a handsome palace built from great blocks of ruby, using all her magic to help the people and never harming anyone who was good. Everyone loved her, but her greatest sorrow was that she could find no one to love in return, since all the men were said to be too stupid and ugly to mate with one so beautiful and wise. At last she found a boy who was handsome, manly, and wise beyond his years; she took him to her ruby palace and used her magic to make him as strong and good and lovely as any woman could wish, resolving to make him her husband once he grew to manhood.

## Biography

The City of Emeralds is spoken of as the home of a being more powerful than the Wicked Witches, and it becomes the destination Dorothy is instructed to reach. A magic slate names it as the place she must go, and she sets about preparing for the journey there, gathering fruit and water and readying her one spare dress.

## Events

Using a magic slate, the Witch of the North determines that Dorothy must travel to the City of Emeralds to seek help from Oz, the Great Wizard.

page.title: Guardian of the Gates
page.content:
## Biography

The Guardian of the Gates is an officer of the Emerald City who lives in a room by its gate and is responsible for admitting travelers. When Dorothy and her companions first arrive, he unlocks their green spectacles, returns them to his great box, and opens the gate for them. Asked which road leads to the Wicked Witch of the West, he answers that there is no road, since no one ever wishes to go that way; on learning the travelers mean to destroy her, he remarks that this is different, as he had assumed she would make slaves of them as she has of others. When the group returns to the Emerald City after Dorothy melts the Wicked Witch of the West, the Guardian of the Gates greets them again, surprised at their return, and it is through him that the people of the city first learn of the Witch's defeat.

## Infobox

- Place type: Boundary region / meadow
- Region: Between the Country of the Winkies and the territory of the Emerald City

## Biography

This place marks the boundary between the Country of the Winkies and the territory of the Emerald City, the crossing point being a river spanned by a high bridge. Around it lies a wide green meadow, "as pretty as a well-kept lawn," free of houses or farms. From the top of the bridge, travelers can see far off the spires and domes of the Emerald City rising above its emerald walls, "sparkling like brilliant jewels." The same name also attaches to a great hall within a royal residence, where the shaggy man was received by one of Princess Ozma's servants and offered passage to "your apartments," an offer he accepted.

## Events

Dorothy, the shaggy man, Button-Bright, Toto, and Polychrome, stranded at the edge of the Deadly Desert, are carried across it after the shaggy man summons Johnny Dooit with the Love Magnet to build a sand-boat. The boat crashes into rocks at the desert's far edge, and the travelers land unharmed in the yellow Country of the Winkies. At the Truth Pond, Button-Bright's fox head and the shaggy man's donkey head wash away, restoring their true faces. The group then meets Tik-tok and Billina, who guide them toward the Emerald City, stopping overnight at Nick Chopper's tin castle. Along the road they visit Jack Pumpkinhead at his pumpkin farm and hear the Tin Woodman's account of the Powder of Life. The Cowardly Lion and Hungry Tiger meet the party with Ozma's golden chariot and escort them into the Emerald City and the royal palace, where Ozma's birthday celebration draws many guests. Afterward the Wizard sends several visitors home in magic bubbles, while Dorothy returns to Kansas by the Magic Belt.

## Physical

The meadow surrounding the bridge is described as a green expanse "as pretty as a well-kept lawn," with no houses or farms to break the scene. Feathery trees line both sides of the road near the bridge, into which Polly danced upon crossing. From the bridge, the distant Emerald City appears with magnificent spires and splendid domes towering above emerald walls.

## Trivia

- The shaggy man, on first seeing the distant city from the bridge, "drew a deep breath of awe and amazement," having never dreamed such a place could exist.
- Polly's violet eyes were said to sparkle "like amethysts" when she was pleased by the sight.

## Biography

Boq is a Munchkin encountered at a gathering where people dance. Upon seeing Dorothy's silver shoes, he tells her she must be a great sorceress, and remarks that her blue and white checked dress is kind to wear, noting that blue is the color of the Munchkins and white is the witch color. After Dorothy tires of watching the dancing, Boq leads her into his house and gives her a room with a pretty bed, its sheets made of blue cloth, where she sleeps soundly until morning with Toto curled on the blue rug beside her.

## Biography

The Land of the South is a region that Dorothy resolves to travel to on the Scarecrow's advice, in order to ask Glinda for help returning to Kansas. The Tin Woodman decides to accompany her, offering that his axe may be of service on the journey. The group sets out from the outer gate of the Emerald City, turning their faces toward the Land of the South under bright sunshine, in good spirits as they begin the journey.

Mr. Joker is one of the clowns among the china people, known for constantly trying to stand on his head. He has broken himself so often in this pursuit that he is mended in a hundred places, leaving him, as the china lady notes, not at all pretty. page.title: Scarecrow
page.content:
## Biography

The Scarecrow is a padded, straw-stuffed figure who becomes one of Dorothy's traveling companions along the road of yellow brick toward the Emerald City. His body is stuffed with straw and his hands are padded and clumsy, making delicate tasks such as gathering nuts difficult. He carries a persistent fear that a spark might catch in his straw and burn him, and for this reason he keeps a good distance from open flames, though he was still willing to gather dry leaves to cover Dorothy while she slept.

Unlike his companions, the Scarecrow does not appear to need rest: during a night spent in the Palace of Oz, he remained standing near the doorway of his room until morning, watching a spider spin its web, since lying down brought him no relief and he could not close his eyes. Before setting out toward the country of the Winkies, he restuffed himself with fresh straw and had Dorothy repaint his eyes so that he could see better.

The Scarecrow's stated wish is to receive brains, which he travels to ask of the Wizard of Oz, telling him he comes praying to have brains put in his head. He also declares, alongside his companions, an intention to destroy the Wicked Witch of the West rather than be made her slave. During the journey he performed a number of practical roles: he seized Dorothy's oil-can to help free the rusted jaw of the Tin Woodman, gathered nuts and fruit to feed Dorothy, and, together with the Tin Woodman, helped steady and pole a raft across a river, though the current swept the raft away and left him clinging to his pole in the middle of the river. He was later separated from the group, his clothing tossed into a tall tree, from which his companions eventually recovered it by chopping the tree down.

The Scarecrow was also present when Dorothy was rescued by the Queen of the Field Mice, formally introducing the two, and he helped push the mice's truck to pull the sleeping Cowardly Lion clear of the poppy field. According to Dorothy's account of events she later related to the Tin Woodman, the Scarecrow, when the group was attacked by crows sent by the Wicked Witch of the West, twisted the neck of each bird in turn and emerged unharmed.

## Narrative role

The Scarecrow is first found by Dorothy stuck on a pole in a cornfield, winking and speaking to her; she frees him from the pole, and he joins her journey in the hope that Oz will give him brains. Traveling together, the Scarecrow maintains that brains matter more than a heart for happiness, holding this view even as a companion who has lost his ability to love a Munchkin girl he once wished to marry comes to believe that happiness requires a heart instead. He and Dorothy also share a quieter moment, finding water and eating breakfast together before hearing groans from the forest.

Crossing a river on a raft, the Scarecrow's pole sticks fast in the riverbed, leaving him stranded alone in the middle of the river as the raft drifts on without him; a Stork agrees to help him, lifting him by the arms and carrying him back to his companions. He is later restuffed with clean straw and joyfully reunited with his friends. Continuing on, he, Dorothy, Tin Woodman, and Cowardly Lion become lost together in fields of buttercups and daisies while trying to find their way back to the Emerald City.

In the Emerald City, Oz delays receiving the Scarecrow for days, until the Scarecrow threatens to summon the Winged Monkeys; he is eventually admitted to receive his promised brains, and Oz removes his head, fills it with bran mixed with pins and needles, and reattaches it. When Oz prepares to depart in his balloon, lighting a fire beneath it to fill it with hot air, he declares that the Scarecrow will rule the Emerald City in his absence, and the Scarecrow duly becomes its ruler, with its people taking pride in being governed by a stuffed man.

Afterward, the Scarecrow joins Tin Woodman and Cowardly Lion in praising Oz, while Dorothy privately forgives him for not keeping his promise, and the Guardian tells the Scarecrow that he must return to rule the Emerald City once Dorothy is safely home. Setting out again, the Scarecrow is seized by the first row of trees at the edge of a thick forest and flung back when he tries to pass beneath them; later, when the group cannot pull up a heavy ladder, they let him fall first and land on him to reach the ground safely. Before being brought before Glinda, who sits on a throne of rubies, the Scarecrow tidies himself alongside Dorothy, Tin Woodman, and Cowardly Lion.

## Personality

The Scarecrow shows a readiness to own his mistakes: after oiling the Tin Woodman's jaws too hastily leaves him fumbling, he remarks it "will serve me a lesson ... to look where I step," treating the error as something to learn from rather than brush aside. His care for his companions comes through in small, unasked-for gestures — gathering nuts for Dorothy's basket and covering her with dry leaves as she sleeps, acts Dorothy herself calls "very kind and thoughtful" — even though his clumsy, padded hands make such simple tasks awkward.

A quiet, practical caution shapes his movements: he deliberately keeps his distance from campfires, fearing a stray spark might catch his straw, a wariness that governs how closely he can approach warmth others take for granted. He is also formally courteous under pressure, addressing the Queen of the Field Mice with "Permit me to introduce to you her Majesty, the Queen." This same disposition tips into stubborn resolve when pushed: crossing the river, he keeps driving his pole against the current toward the Emerald City until it sticks fast in the mud, leaving him stranded rather than let go early. Left alone for a night in the palace, he does not seek comfort or rest but simply stands within the doorway until morning, staring at a spider — a passive, undemanding patience that needs neither sleep nor company to pass the time.

## Appearance

The Scarecrow's body is filled with straw, and he periodically restuffs himself with fresh straw before setting out on a journey. His hands are padded and clumsy, making delicate tasks difficult — when gathering nuts for Dorothy, he drops almost as many as he manages to place in her basket. His eyes are painted rather than natural; on one occasion Dorothy applied new paint to them so that he might see better. He wears clothes that can be separated from his straw-filled form, as shown when the Winged Monkeys tossed his clothing into the branches of a tall tree, leaving him without them until they were later recovered. Because his body is packed with straw, he is wary of open flame, fearing that a stray spark could catch in the straw and burn him.

## Powers

The Scarecrow has no magic, but his straw-and-cloth construction sets him apart from ordinary companions: he needs neither food nor sleep, standing motionless through an entire night without lying down or closing his eyes. This same construction is also his chief vulnerability — he keeps a careful distance from open flame, fearing a stray spark could catch in his straw and burn him up. His padded hands, while clumsy for fine work such as gathering nuts, do not stop him from performing sustained physical labor, such as pushing a pole to steady a raft against a river current.

## Relationships

**[[Dorothy]]** — friend. Their journey together suggests a close friendship: the Scarecrow filled Dorothy's basket with nuts so that she "would not be hungry for a long time," and kept away from the campfire himself for fear of sparks, only to draw near again and "cover Dorothy with dry leaves when she lay down to sleep."

**[[Tin Woodman]]** — friend. The bond between the two seems to run deep: when the Scarecrow was carried off by the Winged Monkeys and lost, the Tin Woodman lamented, "If we only had the Scarecrow with us again, I should be quite happy," prompting the group to search for him. Before that loss, the pair worked side by side, standing together at one end of the raft to steady it while crossing the river.

**[[Cowardly Lion]]** — friend. Their relationship seems to have begun roughly — the Lion once sent the Scarecrow "spinning over and over" upon their first encounter — yet the two are later found labouring and travelling as companions, pushing together to free the truck carrying the sleeping Lion from the poppy field and continuing side by side toward the Emerald City.

**[[Wizard]]** — employment. The connection appears transactional, centred on the Scarecrow's plea to Oz: "I come to you praying that you will put brains in my head."

**[[Wicked Witch]]** — enemy. Their relation seems adversarial: warned that the Witch would find and enslave the travelers, the Scarecrow answered, "we mean to destroy her."

## Trivia

- Left alone in a room of the Palace of Oz, the Scarecrow could not rest by lying down or close his eyes, so he spent the entire night standing in the doorway watching a spider weave its web in a corner.
- His body being stuffed with straw, he kept a careful distance from open flame, fearing that a stray spark might catch and burn him.
- When the Wicked Witch sent forty crows to peck out the eyes of the travelers, the Scarecrow defended the group by seizing each crow and twisting its neck.
- Before the group set out again for the Emerald City, he restuffed himself with fresh straw, and Dorothy repainted his eyes so that he might see better.

page.title: The Scarecrow
page.content:
## Biography

The Scarecrow, also called the King, rules the Emerald City, having been invited by its people to become their ruler, just as the Winkies invited the Tin Woodman to rule them. He is remembered as a friend of Dorothy, the girl who was blown to the Land of Oz from Kansas by a cyclone; the Scarecrow and the Tin Woodman accompanied her during her travels there. Addressed as "His Majesty the Scarecrow" and "your majesty," his straw-stuffed body leaves him vulnerable to fire: when Mombi sent a sheet of crackling flame across a meadow, he became afraid for the first time and turned to flee, trembling until his straw rattled.

His rule was interrupted when General Jinjur's all-girl Army of Revolt conquered the Emerald City after his Standing Army fled rather than fight; he received the news of the city's fall calmly. Having escaped the city, he later returned to restore order, remarking that governing had grown burdensome for the men left doing housework and minding the children in his absence. He is thoughtful and cautious by nature — he often pauses to think through a problem in silence, grows uneasy when soldiers of the Army of Revolt let his group pass without resistance, suspecting a trap, and distrusts anything that seems "too easy."

## Relationships

**[[Nick Chopper]]** — friend. Their bond seems close: excerpts describe the Scarecrow and the Tin Woodman accompanying Dorothy together on her travels, and General Jinjur's fear that "his Majesty and the Tin Woodman Joined forces" would endanger her rebellion suggests the two acted as allies against her.

**[[Tip]]** — friend. Tip appears to be an ally, describing the Scarecrow to Jack Pumpkinhead as "Another friend of Dorothy's," and, according to Jack Pumpkinhead's account, cutting him free after the Saw-Horse's river accident left him collapsed on the bank.

**[[Woggle-Bug]]** — friend. Their exchange — "Are you really a Woggle-Bug?" enquired the Scarecrow — and his joining Nick Chopper in warning the Woggle-Bug to restrain his punning suggest a cordial, if exasperated, familiarity.

**[[General Jinjur]]** — enemy. Jinjur's Army of Revolt conquers the Emerald City specifically to unseat "His Majesty the Scarecrow," and her subsequent effort to enlist Mombi to prevent his return indicates an antagonistic relationship.

**[[Jack Pumpkinhead]]** — friend. According to Tip's account, the two are found together playing quoits when news of the city's fall arrives, and the Scarecrow reacts calmly in his presence, suggesting an easy familiarity.

page.title: Scarecrow
page.content:
## Biography

The Scarecrow attends a private gathering in the drawing-room of Ozma's palace, seated between Tiktok and the Tin Woodman, opposite Ozma and Princess Langwidere. When Langwidere complains that she cannot bear heat, he remarks that heat suits her, joking that she would be "better than ever" if nicely roasted. He travels by riding on the back of the Sawhorse rather than walking.

According to an account given before Ozma, the Scarecrow was once driven from the throne of the Emerald City by an army of women assembled by Jinjur, who later fought a battle against the army of Glinda the Sorceress. On another occasion, upon being reunited with the Tin Woodman, the Scarecrow throws himself upon "the bosom of his old comrade," surprised and delighted to see him again, while Tiktok also greets the Tin Woodman warmly before the group makes way for Ozma to welcome him and the army cheers. At a feast held for the army's officers, the Scarecrow — evidently well acquainted with the palace staff — pinches the cheek of the maid Jellia Jamb.

## Relationships

**[[Dorothy]]** — friend. The two seem close, having spent an afternoon talking together along with the Tin Woodman.

**[[Tin Woodman]]** — friend. Long-standing comrades: the Scarecrow addresses him as "old friend," and upon their reunion after separation he threw himself upon his old comrade's bosom in delight.

**[[Ozma]]** — friend. Ozma appears to hold the Scarecrow in trust, seating him near her so that she might ask his advice about the journey.

**[[King]]** — enemy. The pairing suggests an adversarial relationship, though the surviving record does not detail a direct confrontation between them.

**[[Nome King]]** — enemy. The Scarecrow joined Ozma's expedition against the Nome King's underground realm, undertaken to free the enslaved Queen of Ev and her children.

contributions.title: Dorothy and the Wizard in Oz

page.title: Scarecrow
page.content:
## Biography

The Scarecrow is a straw man of the Land of Oz, regarded there as an important personage. Made of stuffed, padded material, with soft stuffed hands, he owes his brains to the Wizard, a gift he prizes highly, claiming they let him think day and night, when all other brains are fast asleep. He is counted among Dorothy's old friends: he is remembered as having helped her, together with the Tin Woodman, in past struggles against enemies such as the Wicked Witch and the Nome King. On Dorothy's return to Oz, the Scarecrow rushes in to hug her in his padded arms, glad to see her again. He later takes part in the affairs of the court, expressing dismay over the arrest of the kitten Eureka and serving among the nine members chosen for her jury alongside the Cowardly Lion, the Hungry Tiger, Jim, the Yellow Hen, the Wizard, Tik-tok, the Sawhorse, and Zeb.

## Relationships

**[[DOROTHY]]** — ally. This bond seems tied to past struggles faced together, as the Wizard recalls that "you had the Scarecrow and the Tin Woodman to help you conquer those enemies."

**[[WIZARD]]** — friend. Their friendship is suggested by the Wizard grasping "the soft, stuffed hands of his old friend," a gesture consistent with long familiarity.

**[[Sawhorse]]** — acquaintance. A familiar rapport seems indicated when the Scarecrow suggests he could "race with the Sawhorse."

**[[Woggle-Bug]]** — friendly rivalry. Their connection could indicate a lighthearted rivalry, both being present at Princess Ozma's court proceedings — the Scarecrow seated among the jury while the Woggle-Bug addressed it as Public Accuser.

page.title: Scarecrow
page.content:
## Biography

The Scarecrow is a well-known figure whose expected absence is a matter of concern before Ozma's birthday festivities: Dorothy anxiously hopes he will not be late, and Ozma reassures her that he is sure to return the next day. Described as "the famous Scarecrow," he arrives in the Emerald City riding proudly upon the back of the wooden Saw-Horse, which pranced along the street almost as gracefully as if it had been made of flesh, its wooden legs shod with plates of solid gold and its saddle richly embroidered and glittering with jewels. His arrival is met by a band of musicians and crowds of people who cheer so lustily that they nearly drown out the drums and horns.

Upon reaching the palace, the Scarecrow looks up, sees Dorothy, and waves his peaked hat at her in greeting before dismounting at the front door, after which the band stops playing and the crowds disperse to their dwellings.

## Relationships

**[[Dorothy]]** — friend. A remark that "I came here once with my friends the Scarecrow, and the Tin Woodman" suggests a longstanding friendship between them, and Dorothy's anxious wait for his return points to the same bond.

**[[Button-Bright]]** — acquaintance. Button-Bright seems "wonderfully attracted by the straw man," hinting at a passing fascination rather than a deep tie.

**[[John Dough]]** — acquaintance. A shared assurance that visitors "will be perfectly safe while you remain in Oz" places the two only loosely in the same circle.

**[[Nick Chopper]]** — friend. Their connection is suggested only by association among Oz's companions.

**[[Polly]]** — acquaintance. Their link appears only as a faint association, with no further detail given.

page.content:
## Biography

The Scarecrow is counted among the old friends of the Wizard, alongside the Tin Woodman and Jack Pumpkinhead. Originally he was a farmer, having passed his early life in a cornfield, where he was supposed to frighten away the crows. He once marched with Dorothy and her army to the Nome King's underground cavern beyond the Land of Ev, and during that expedition he nearly frightened King Roquat into fits by throwing one of Billina's eggs at him. The Scarecrow and Dorothy once found the Tin Woodman rusted still in the woods and oiled his joints, after which the three traveled together to visit the Wizard at the Emerald City. According to the Tin Woodman, the Scarecrow cannot be contented with city life, however beautiful the surroundings might be.

page.title: Tin Woodman
page.content:
## Biography

The Tin Woodman, also known simply as the Woodman, is a companion of Dorothy on her journey along the road of yellow brick toward the Emerald City, traveling alongside the Scarecrow and, later, the Cowardly Lion and the dog Toto. He admits to never having been to the Emerald City himself, though his father made the journey once when he was a boy and reported it as long and passing through dangerous country, growing more beautiful nearer the city where Oz dwells. The Woodman knows that he has no heart, and for that reason takes great care never to be cruel or unkind to anything, walking carefully so as not to even harm a passing ant; as he puts it, those with hearts have something to guide them, but having none, he must be especially careful.

His care extends to protecting his companions and the creatures around him: he holds Toto back from chasing the field mice, refuses to kill a deer for food for fear that weeping over it would rust his jaws, and carries an oil-can to keep his joints moving. He performs much of the group's practical labor, chopping wood for their camp with his axe and building the raft of logs and wooden pins used to cross a wide river that blocked their path, standing at one end with the Scarecrow to steady it with long poles. When a great Wildcat comes bounding after a small mouse who turns out to be the Queen of the Field Mice, he kills the beast with his axe, and afterward helps push the mice's truck to safety. His head, which turns on hinges, and his tin body serve him well: when the Scarecrow later scatters his own straw over Dorothy, Toto, and the Lion to shield them from the Wicked Witch's bees, the bees find only the Woodman to sting and break all their stingers against his tin without harming him at all.

## Relationships

**[[Scarecrow]]** — friend. Their bond seems to run through repeated support on the road, suggested by the Scarecrow greeting him "heartily" with "Come along."

**[[Dorothy]]** — friend. The tie between them could indicate mutual gratitude, hinted at by her remark that he "certainly saved" her life.

**[[Cowardly Lion]]** — friend. Despite the Lion striking at him with his "sharp claws" during an early encounter in the forest, the blow left him unharmed, which suggests the friendship endured past this clash.

**[[Wizard]]** — employment. Their connection appears tied to the shared purpose of the journey toward the Emerald City to seek an audience with Oz, though the excerpts offer only limited grounding for the nature of this bond.

**[[Wicked Witch]]** — enemy. Their opposition seems evident when she sends a pack of wolves against the travelers, which he destroys with his axe.

page.title: Nick Chopper
page.content:
## Biography

Nick Chopper, generally known as the Tin Woodman and called Nick by his companions, rules the West Country of the Winkies, a land where everything is yellow. He was invited to become the Winkies' ruler after he helped Dorothy destroy the Wicked Witch of the West, an act for which the grateful Winkies offered him the throne; he styles himself their Emperor.

Before assuming this rule, Nick Chopper accompanied Dorothy, a girl carried to the Land of Oz from Kansas by a cyclone, and the Scarecrow on her travels through the country. Among his remembered deeds from that period is the destruction of the Wicked Witch's Grey Wolves.

When General Jinjur's Army of Revolt drove the Scarecrow from the Emerald City, the Tin Woodman reacted to the news with alarm, calling it a calamity, and resolved to march at once to recapture the city and restore the Scarecrow to his throne. He undertook this journey together with Tip, Jack Pumpkinhead, and the Saw-Horse, a company later joined along the road by the Woggle-Bug. The march toward the Emerald City was thrown off course when the witch Mombi, summoned by Jinjur to stop the group, worked magic from a tower room that left the Tin Woodman certain they had lost their way despite his knowing every step of the route.

During the journey, the Tin Woodman performed the operation of amputating Jack Pumpkinhead's wooden leg and fitting it, cut down to size, onto the Saw-Horse.

## Narrative role

Nick Chopper, known as the Tin Woodman, enters the narrative as Emperor of the Winkies, ruling the western country and named as the destination the Scarecrow turns to for protection when driven from the [[Emerald City]]. Retracing the road together, the Scarecrow recalls an earlier adventure in which Nick Chopper destroyed the Wicked Witch's Grey Wolves alongside Dorothy, a deed remembered as one of the notable feats of their shared travels. Once reunited with the Scarecrow's party, the Tin Woodman resolves to help retake the Emerald City without raising a large army. The group's journey is soon disrupted: the Tin Woodman notices that something has gone wrong with their route, and the travelers find themselves surrounded by a field of giant sunflowers bearing girls' faces, a sight they suspect is the work of Mombi's magic. When Jack Pumpkinhead's leg is damaged, Nick Chopper amputates it and refits it to the Saw-Horse, prompting a round of bickering between Jack and the Saw-Horse before the group resumes its travel. Further along, the Tin Woodman blows a silver whistle to summon the Queen of the Field Mice, an old friend whose life he once saved.

Leading the march on the Emerald City, the Tin Woodman wields his axe to frighten off the guards of the Army of Revolt, and the travelers enter the city unopposed — only for General Jinjur to signal her Army of Revolt to surround and disarm them, seizing the Tin Woodman's axe and taking the group prisoner. Held captive, the party regroups around a plan: the Scarecrow proposes building a flying machine on the palace roof and animating it with the Powder of Life, naming the Tin Woodman as its builder, and Nick Chopper also repairs Jack Pumpkinhead's broken leg with a table leg before the group disperses to gather materials. Assembling on the roof, the travelers collect a Gump's head with antlers, two sofas, a broom, ropes, and four palm-tree leaves cut by the Tin Woodman, who then designs the machine itself, binding the two sofas together as its body and attaching the Gump's head to the front. Before the machine departs, the travelers fall unharmed into a hidden Jackdaw's nest full of stolen treasures, where the Woggle-Bug gives a found diamond necklace to the Tin Woodman; the Gump then flies south carrying Tip, the Scarecrow, the Tin Woodman, Jack Pumpkinhead, the Woggle-Bug, and the Saw-Horse.

Later, unaware of its true identity, the Tin Woodman plucks a rose and pins it to his chest as a search party withdraws in defeat — the rose being Mombi in disguise, who believes herself safe hidden in the Tin Woodman's button-hole since no one suspects the two are the same. As the Scarecrow and the Tin Woodman each propose alternate plans, Glinda the Good notices the rose trembling and comes to suspect it is Mombi in disguise. Afterward, the Tin Woodman prepares to return to the Winkie Country, taking the Scarecrow with him to serve as his Royal Treasurer.

## Personality

Nick Chopper shows a protective, take-charge instinct toward his friends. On learning that the Scarecrow had been driven from the Emerald City, he reacts with alarm — "Great Goodness! What a calamity!" — and immediately moves to action, declaring "we must not give them time to do that... we will go at once and recapture the Emerald City." The Scarecrow's own confidence that "he will protect me" if danger comes reflects this same protective reputation.

He is also inclined to speak generously of others: describing a tailor who made Jack Pumpkinhead's clothes, he calls him "a good-hearted tailor, at any rate," giving credit even where the Scarecrow voices mere envy. This generosity extends to practical helpfulness — he agrees to amputate and refit Jack Pumpkinhead's leg onto the Saw-Horse when asked, undertaking the unpleasant task without protest even as the Saw-Horse complains of being "butchered."

According to the traveling party's own account of events, the Tin Woodman also shows a degree of vanity about his appearance, having recently had himself nickel-plated — though this detail rests on the party's subjective retelling rather than direct testimony from Nick Chopper himself.

## Powers

Nick Chopper's combat capability is considerable: the Scarecrow recalls the spot where Nick Chopper destroyed the Wicked Witch's Grey Wolves, a feat tied directly to his standing among the Winkies before he became their ruler. He also possesses a craftsman's precision consistent with his identity as the Tin Woodman: he amputated Jack Pumpkinhead's wooden leg and whittled it down to fit the Saw-Horse, an operation exact enough that the new leg held in place despite the Saw-Horse's complaints about the fit.

## Relationships

**[[The Scarecrow]]** — friend. Nick Chopper is remembered alongside the Scarecrow as one of those who "helped Dorothy to destroy the Wicked Witch of the West," and the Scarecrow later turns to him for protection when driven from the Emerald City, calling him "my friend the Tin Woodman" — a pattern that suggests a lasting friendship between them.

**[[Woggle-Bug]]** — friend. When the Woggle-Bug is met on the road, Nick Chopper welcomes him with "We are bound for the Emerald City now... you are welcome to travel in our company," an invitation that suggests a friendly rapport growing between them.

**[[Tip]]** — friend. Tip travels in Nick Chopper's company and hears him addressed familiarly as "my dear Nick" while he works on Jack Pumpkinhead's leg, which suggests an easy, friendly footing between them.

**[[Jack Pumpkinhead]]** — acquaintance. At Jack's urging — "Get to work, my dear Nick, and fit the Pumpkinhead's leg to the Saw-Horse" — Nick Chopper amputates and refits Jack's leg onto the Saw-Horse, an exchange that suggests a working acquaintance between them rather than a deeper bond.

**[[Glinda the Good]]** — friend. A remark that "I know Glinda the Good, and believe she will prove a friend indeed" could indicate a friendly connection between Nick Chopper and Glinda the Good, though the excerpts do not show them interacting directly.

## Trivia

- Nick Chopper destroyed the Wicked Witch of the West's Grey Wolves, a feat the Scarecrow recalls when Tip asks who Nick Chopper is.
- The Scarecrow addresses him familiarly as "Nick," as when he asks him to fit Jack Pumpkinhead's leg to the Saw-Horse.
- Nick Chopper performed the operation himself, amputating Jack Pumpkinhead's wooden leg and whittling it down to fit the Saw-Horse — an operation the Saw-Horse later complained of as having been "butchered."

page.title: Tin Woodman
page.content:
## Biography

The Tin Woodman is a companion of Ozma of Oz, seated among her court alongside the Scarecrow and Tiktok during palace audiences. He commands the Army of Oz, describing it as composed of eight Generals, six Colonels, seven Majors, five Captains, and a small handful of privates. He takes part in Ozma's processions, marching side by side with Tiktok just behind the Scarecrow. According to Billina, the Tin Woodman was at one point trapped after Prince Evring accidentally pocketed his enchanted whistle, and was restored the instant it was blown.

## Relationships

**[[Ozma]]** — employment. The Tin Woodman speaks of Ozma as ruler and addresses an assembly on her behalf, which suggests he serves under her.

**[[DOROTHY]]** — friend. His frequent presence alongside Dorothy in the palace and on the march could suggest a close acquaintance.

**[[Scarecrow]]** — friend. He is seated and marches beside the Scarecrow, and the two are described as joyfully reunited after a separation, suggesting a close companionship.

**[[Nome King]]** — enemy. He addresses the assembly on the matter of captives held by the Nome King, which suggests an adversarial standing between them.

**[[BILLINA]]** — acquaintance. Their shared presence among the same company suggests only a slight acquaintance.

## Biography

The Tin Woodman is remembered fondly as one of the friends of Oz's former Wizard. Skilled with an axe, he once cut a straight, strong limb from a tree and used it to fashion a new leg and ear for the Sawhorse after the Sawhorse was injured. The Wizard treats him as a trusted friend, privately asking him to defend Dorothy's kitten Eureka when she stands accused of eating Princess Ozma's missing piglet. The Tin Woodman also speaks directly to Eureka, warning her that she may be sorry if she continues to act foolishly.

## Relationships

**[[Sawhorse]]** — friend. His mending of the Sawhorse's broken leg and ear with his axe suggests a friendly bond between them.

page.title: Nick Chopper
page.content:
## Biography

Nick Chopper, known as the Tin Woodman, is a tin man who possesses a heart given to him by the Wizard. After a witch who had enslaved the Winkies was destroyed with a bucket of water, the freed people made Nick Chopper their Emperor. According to Billina, the Tin Woodman's heart grows softer and kindlier every day.

## Narrative role

Nick Chopper, known as the Tin Woodman, is met when Tik-tok and Billina guide the travelers toward the Emerald City; the party stops overnight at Nick Chopper's tin castle along the way. The journey later brings them to Jack Pumpkinhead's pumpkin farm, where Nick Chopper recounts his own account of the Powder of Life.

## Personality

Nick Chopper's most attested trait is a marked and deepening kindness of heart. Dorothy credits him with "a lovely heart," a gift given to him by the Wizard, and Billina reports that this heart "gets softer and kindlier every day," suggesting an ongoing cultivation of tenderness rather than a fixed disposition. The concern others show for him — Dorothy's eagerness to see him again and her pointed question, "how's his heart?" — reflects the warmth he inspires in his companions.

## Appearance

Nick Chopper, also known as the Tin Woodman, is made of tin, a fact reflected in how others refer to him — as "the tin man." No further physical details are given beyond his tin construction.

## Powers

Nick Chopper possesses a heart given to him by the Wizard, described as growing "softer and kindlier every day." This heart sets him apart from ordinary beings, marking him as a figure whose inner nature is not fixed at creation but continues to develop over time.

## Relationships

**[[Dorothy]]** — friend. Dorothy counts Nick Chopper among her old companions, recalling that she "came here once with my friends the Scarecrow, and the Tin Woodman," and later asks after him with warmth, wishing "to see dear Nick Chopper again."

**[[THE shaggy man]]** — friend. The bond seems to form quickly, as he "loved the shaggy man" even before knowing of the Love Magnet, suggesting an easy, immediate friendship.

**[[Jack Pumpkinhead]]** — friend. Nick Chopper appears protective toward Jack Pumpkinhead, declaring "So you shall, since he is still alive. Come with me to his house," which points to a caring, friendly regard.

**[[Tik-tok]]** — friend. The copper man and the tin man are described as "good friends," indicating an easy companionship between the two mechanical figures.

**[[Wizard]]** — other. Nick Chopper's defining feature, his heart, was "given him by the wonderful Wizard," tying the two together, though the excerpts say little of their relationship beyond this gift.

## Trivia

- After Dorothy melted the witch who held them captive, the freed people made Nick Chopper their Emp'ror.
- According to Billina, the heart given to Nick Chopper by the Wizard grows softer and kindlier every day.

## Biography

Nick Chopper, also known as the Tin Woodman, is a companion of Dorothy and resides in a tin castle in Winkie Country. According to Dorothy, she and the Scarecrow once found him rusted stiff in the woods; after oiling his joints until they were slippery again, he accompanied them to visit the Wizard at the Emerald City. He is counted among the friends the Wizard's party plans to call upon on their travels, alongside Jack Pumpkinhead and the Scarecrow — of whom the Tin Woodman remarks that their dear Scarecrow cannot be contented with city life however beautiful his surroundings, noting that the Scarecrow originally passed his early life as a farmer in a cornfield, set there to frighten away crows.

During a visit to his tin castle, where his guests toured his tin gardens and fish pond, the Tin Woodman reported that Ozma had seen in her Magic Picture that the Nome King had dug a tunnel under the desert to invade Oz together with the Whimsies, the Growleywogs, and the Phanfasms.

## Relationships

**[[Scarecrow]]** — friend. Referred to by Nick Chopper as "our dear Scarecrow," the bond seems close, having been forged when Dorothy and the Scarecrow found him rusted still in the woods, oiled his joints, and afterward traveled with him to the Emerald City.

**[[Dorothy]]** — friend. According to Dorothy, she and the Scarecrow found the Tin Woodman rusted still in the woods and got his joints slippery again, after which he went with them to visit the Wizard — suggesting a friendship formed through that rescue.

**[[Ozma]]** — friend. The bond seems to carry some trust, as the Tin Woodman is the one who conveys to the group what Ozma saw in her Magic Picture regarding the Nome King's tunnel under the desert.

**[[Aunt Em]]** — acquaintance. Their connection appears slight, limited to Aunt Em's passing question about lunching "on tin" when the Wizard announces a visit to the Tin Woodman.

**[[General Guph]]** — acquaintance. Their association seems limited, with no direct interaction recorded beyond both figuring in the same traveling party's plans.

page.title: Cowardly Lion
page.content:
## Biography

The Cowardly Lion, also known simply as the Lion or the Lion, is one of Dorothy's traveling companions on the road of yellow brick, joining her in the hope that Oz can give him courage he believes he lacks: "Do you think Oz could give me courage?" he asks, to which the Scarecrow answers that Oz could grant it "Just as easily as he could give me brains." Despite the name he carries, the Lion repeatedly proves capable and useful to the group: he measures a wide ditch and carries Dorothy, the Scarecrow, and the Tin Woodman across on his back one at a time, and later swims to shore towing the raft by his tail after the current sweeps the party away from the road. He hunts for his own food in secret rather than ask Dorothy to prepare cooked meat for him, and by his own admission is "really a wild beast."

The Wizard tells him that as long as the Wicked Witch of the West lives, he must remain a coward, a verdict that angers the Lion, though he says nothing in reply and rushes from the throne room when the Wizard's Ball of Fire grows too hot to face. Yet it is the Lion who scares away the Witch's slaves, one of the events that leaves her without the means to destroy Dorothy and her friends. After the Witch is melted, the Lion reports the news to a man they meet, stating gravely that it was Dorothy who melted her. When the Tin Woodman describes his new heart as kinder than his old one, the Lion declares in turn that he is afraid of nothing on earth and would gladly face an army or a dozen fierce Kalidahs. When the group must later choose whether to stay in the Emerald City or move on, the Lion decides to go with Dorothy, saying he is tired of the city and longs for the woods and country again.

## Relationships

**[[Dorothy]]** — friend. When she declares she is heading to see Oz, the Lion asks whether Oz could give him courage, showing he travels alongside her in pursuit of his own goal.

**[[Scarecrow]]** — friend. The two coordinate closely on the road, with the Scarecrow reasoning out plans — such as having the Lion carry the group across a wide ditch on his back, one at a time — and the Lion executing them.

**[[Tin Woodman]]** — friend. The Woodman stands with the Scarecrow at one end of the raft to steady it while the Lion's weight tips it, and later the Lion swims the group to shore by towing the raft with his tail while the Woodman helps pole it.

**[[Wizard]]** — employment. This connection seems tied to the Lion's audience with the Wizard, in which he is told he must remain a coward as long as the Witch lives, a verdict that visibly angers him before he flees the room.

**[[Toto]]** — friend. Their bond appears secondary to the Lion's ties with Dorothy's human companions, though he travels as part of the same company as the dog throughout the journey.

**[[Wicked Witch]]** — enemy. The Witch loses her slaves specifically because they are scared away by the Cowardly Lion, suggesting he plays a direct part in dismantling her remaining forces before her end.

**[[Glinda]]** — acquaintance. Evidence for this bond is too slight to state anything beyond its bare existence.

page.title: Cowardly Lion
page.content:
## Biography

The Cowardly Lion, also known simply as the Lion, rules the great forest as the King of Beasts. He knew nothing of Ozma until she became the reigning princess of Oz, after which he journeyed to the Emerald City to see her. On learning that she was about to visit the Land of Ev to set free its royal family, he begged to go with her and brought along his friend, the Hungry Tiger.

Despite his royal title, the Lion shows open unease when confronted with danger: faced with a great hammer swinging near his head, he shuddered and admitted it made him "dreadfully nervous."

## Relationships

**[[DOROTHY]]** — friend. He seems to have looked in on her at one point to try to comfort her, suggesting a caring bond between them.

**[[Ozma]]** — ally. His request to accompany her to the Land of Ev suggests a loyalty to her cause.

**[[Tiger]]** — friend. He is described as bringing along his friend the Hungry Tiger when joining the expedition.

**[[Nome King]]** — enemy. His role in the expedition to free the Ev royal family seems to place him in opposition to the Nome King, who holds them prisoner.

page.title: Wicked Witch
page.content:
## Biography

The Wicked Witch rules a country in the west inhabited by the Winkies, holding them in bondage until her death. She has one eye that can see far off, which she uses to spot travelers crossing her territory. She commands a silver whistle that summons a swarm of black bees, and she can direct wolves and crows to attack intruders, ordering the King Crow to "peck out their eyes and tear them to pieces." She once enchanted the axe of a woodman, causing it to cut off his limbs and head one by one. When her wolves and crows are destroyed by the travelers, she flies into a terrible rage. Dorothy eventually destroys her by throwing a bucket of water over her, melting her entirely; afterward the Winkies, freed from her rule, wish for the Tin Woodman to govern them in her place. Munchkins in the east also celebrate their freedom from the bondage of a Wicked Witch, killed by Dorothy's house falling upon her, after which Dorothy is given the dead witch's silver shoes.

## Relationships

**[[Dorothy]]** — enemy. Wolves, crows, and bees were sent against Dorothy and her companions, suggesting deep hostility toward her; the conflict seems to have ended with the Witch's destruction, as Dorothy recounts having "melted her with a bucket of water."

**[[Tin Woodman]]** — enemy. An account attributed to the Tin Woodman suggests the Witch once enchanted his axe, causing it to sever his arms and head one by one.

**[[Scarecrow]]** — enemy. Crows sent by the Witch attacked the travelers, but the Scarecrow reportedly twisted each bird's neck and survived unharmed, an episode that could indicate direct opposition between them.

**[[Cowardly Lion]]** — enemy. The Lion is told that only proof of the Witch's death will grant him courage, suggesting an antagonistic tie between the two.

**[[Toto]]** — enemy. Toto travels among those the Witch's wolves, crows, and bees are sent against, which could indicate he too is counted among her targets.

## Infobox

- Name: Munchkins
- Aliases: Munchkin
- Role: Farmers and other inhabitants of a country where blue is the customary color of dress

## Biography

The Munchkins are the people of a country where blue is worn as a matter of custom; those who live there, such as a Munchkin farmer described making a figure for his cornfield, dress in faded blue suits and boots with blue tops, "such as every man wore in this country." This farmer built a straw-stuffed figure with a sack head painted with eyes, nose, and mouth, topping it with an old, pointed blue hat that had belonged to some Munchkin.

While the farmer worked, another Munchkin stood by and offered opinions on the figure's construction, remarking that the painted ears were not straight and later approving of the blue paint chosen for its eye, saying, "Blue paint is just the color for eyes." The finished figure, left standing on a pole among the corn, was mistaken by passing crows for a Munchkin, a mistake it found gratifying.

Among the Munchkins was a girl of notable beauty, whom the Tin Woodman came to love. He resolved to marry her once he had earned enough money to build her a better house, and she in turn promised to marry him once that house was built.

## Biography

This Munchkin is a small figure who, despite standing barely tall enough to reach Zeb's shoulder, seemed to be the wrestling champion among his people during a gathering held before Ozma and her guests. Twice Zeb's apparent age, he wore a peaked hat ringed with little bells that tinkled as he moved, and sported long pointed whiskers. When Zeb wrestled him, the Munchkin threw the boy to the ground three times with apparent ease, prompting Zeb to challenge him to a boxing match instead. That contest ended when Zeb landed a sharp blow to his ears, at which the Munchkin sat down on the ground and cried, his tears running down his whiskers, because he had been hurt.

page.title: Tip
page.content:
## Biography

Tip is a youth of the Country of the Gillikins, in the North of the Land of Oz. Old Mombi, his guardian, sometimes calls him by his longer name, Tippetarius, though he is known simply as Tip. He is also known as Ozma, or Princess Ozma. Tip remembers nothing of his own parents; he was brought to Mombi while still quite young and raised by her, though her reputation was far from good.

Restless and fond of mischief, Tip built a figure from a carved pumpkin and wooden limbs, naming it Jack Pumpkinhead, and hauled it to the bend in the road to give old Mombi a fright. When Mombi later threatened to turn him into a marble statue, Tip refused to accept such a fate. He gathered bread and cheese, took a pepper-box holding the Powder of Life from her basket, and slipped away at night with Jack.

On the road, Tip cared for his companions: he repaired Jack's wooden joints whenever they gave way, and after bringing an old sawhorse to life as the Saw-Horse, he whittled it a pair of ears from bark so it could hear his commands. When a ferryman refused to carry the travelers across a river without payment, the group crossed on their own and continued on toward the Emerald City, the grass and trees turning from lavender to green as they neared it.

Upon reaching the Emerald City, Tip presented Jack Pumpkinhead to His Majesty the Scarecrow, and it was there confirmed, in answer to Jellia's question, that Tip was the one who had made Jack.

## Narrative role

Tip is a Gillikin youth living in the North of Oz as ward of old Mombi, an old woman suspected of practicing magic. He remembers nothing of his parents, having been raised by Mombi since early childhood, and is set to daily chores — cutting wood, tending the corn-fields, keeping pigs, and milking — from which he regularly slacks off to play whenever Mombi's attention is elsewhere. Using branches and clothing found in Mombi's chest, he builds and dresses a figure he names Jack Pumpkinhead.

Later, Tip runs behind the galloping Saw-Horse while holding onto its tail, but the branch he grips breaks and he is left behind on the road. Afterward, when Jack's pumpkin head is swept downstream, Tip retrieves it with a long pole and reattaches it to Jack's neck.

When Jinjur threatens to destroy each of the companions in gruesome fashion, she orders that Tip be returned to old Mombi. Around this time, Tip's Powder of Life falls from his pocket, and he explains that it can bring anything to life but that only one dose remains.

Tip speaks the magic words he learned from Mombi, and the Thing comes to life, screeching and flapping its wings violently. Worried that the powder is running low, he must decide whether to animate the head or the legs of the sofas; he then commands the Gump to return, and because its head has been brought to life, it obeys and lands safely back on the roof.

Tip explains to the newly animated Gump-headed Thing that it exists to carry the group through the air. He also discovers a false bottom in the discarded pepper-box, holding three of Dr. Nikidik's silver wishing pills — useless, since the instructions require counting seventeen by twos. When Jackdaws' stolen money is found in their nest, Tip suggests restuffing the Scarecrow with it, and the group refills him with bills of various denominations.

Old Mombi eventually admits that the Wizard gave her a baby named Ozma in exchange for teaching her magic tricks — an admission that reveals Tip to be that child, also known as Princess Ozma. When Jinjur refuses to give up her throne and declares war on Glinda the Good and Ozma, the Army of Revolt ultimately surrenders and the stolen jewels are returned; Ozma is crowned queen of the Emerald City, and Jinjur despairs on learning that Mombi has confessed and that Tip is truly Princess Ozma.

## Personality

Tip is mischievous and inventive, drawn to testing "the cleverness of his workmanship" rather than to strict practicality; he builds Jack Pumpkinhead expressly to frighten old Mombi and takes evident satisfaction in seeing the trick succeed. This same restless curiosity shows in his willingness to experiment — first with the Powder of Life, later by whittling a pair of ears for the newly awakened Saw-Horse when the creature fails to heed a shouted "Whoa!"

He also shows a rebellious streak toward authority: faced with the prospect of "being a marble statue," he resolves, rebelliously, that "I'm not going to stand it," and admits in private that he "never did like that old woman," Mombi, wondering "how I ever came to live with her." Yet Tip is not merely defiant — he is attentive and conscientious toward what he creates. When Jack's joints give way and he crashes to the ground, Tip rushes to him, straightens his limbs, and checks his head for cracks, and he later regrets not having "constructed the wooden limbs more carefully and substantially." He also proves patient with Jack's oddities, choosing to let the Pumpkinhead call him "father" rather than undertake "another long and tedious explanation." Confronted with sudden mishap, such as the Saw-Horse's wild circling that leaves him "dancing away in pain," Tip reacts with alarm but responds practically, seeking a workable fix rather than giving in to panic.

## Appearance

Tip is described as a boy of small and delicate build, a detail noted when Jack Pumpkinhead addresses him as "father."

## Powers

Tip has no innate magical ability, but shows real skill as a craftsman: he assembles a pumpkin-headed man whose jointed limbs are sturdy enough to walk, working the leg joints by hand until they hold together, and takes visible pride in testing "the cleverness of his workmanship." His capacity to bring a creation to life depends on the Powder of Life, a substance he takes rather than one he possesses by nature — his gift lies in construction and resourceful use of found materials, not in sorcery of his own.

## Relationships

**[[The Scarecrow]]** — friend. Tip's road led toward the Emerald City ruled by the Scarecrow, and Jack Pumpkinhead's introduction of himself as the work of "a boy named Tip" suggests an emerging friendly connection forming between Tip and the Scarecrow.

**[[Jack Pumpkinhead]]** — family. Tip carved and animated Jack with the Powder of Life; Jack repeatedly calls him "father," a title Tip found embarrassing yet never denied, suggesting a father-son-like bond between them.

**[[Nick Chopper]]** — friend. Tip's tie to Nick Chopper seems to come from the same circle gathered around the Scarecrow and the Emerald City, though the bond is only suggested, not shown directly.

**[[Woggle-Bug]]** — acquaintance. Tip questioned the Woggle-Bug directly — "But where were you going, when you met us?" — pointing to at least a passing acquaintance between them.

**[[Saw-Horse]]** — other. Tip whittled ears for the newly animated Saw-Horse so it could hear his commands, and later instructed it to "wiggle your legs" while crossing the river, suggesting a caretaker-like bond with the creature he helped bring to life.

## Trivia

- Old Mombi addressed Tip by his full name, Tippetarius, though the shorter name was used by everyone else.
- When the newly animated Saw-Horse ignored Tip's shouted commands to stop, Jack Pumpkinhead pointed out that the creature had no ears; Tip then whittled a pair from tree bark and fastened them to its head.
- A ferryman refused to row Tip and his companions across the river on the road to the Emerald City because Tip carried no money.
- Tip built Jack Pumpkinhead's wooden joints himself; by the time they reached the Emerald City, the purple trousers, pink waistcoat, and red shirt still hung loosely over the joints he had constructed.
