page.title: Woggle-Bug
page.content:
## Biography

The Woggle-Bug is an insect of extraordinary size, appearing before the Scarecrow, the Tin Woodman, and their companions dressed as a dandy: a dark-blue swallowtail coat with yellow lining, a white duck vest, fawn-colored knickerbockers with gilt buckles, and a tall silk hat. Standing as tall as the Tin Woodman, he is remarked to be larger than any bug ever seen in the Land of Oz. He takes evident pride in his own strangeness, declaring that surprising people affords him pleasure and that he is entitled to curiosity and admiration rather than being classed with ordinary insects.

According to his own account, the Woggle-Bug spent about three years hidden near the hearth of a country school-house, secretly listening to the lectures of Professor Nowitall, and credits this period with the vast learning he claims for himself, styling himself "T.E.", Thoroughly Educated. He travels afterward with the Scarecrow, the Tin Woodman, Tip, Jack Pumpkinhead, and the Saw-Horse, offering frequent, often unwelcome, remarks on puns and education along the way. He is present through the group's confrontation with General Jinjur in the Emerald City, the escape from the palace roof, the building of the flying Thing from two sofas and a Gump's head, and the journey south, during which he complains of sea-sickness and survives an attack by Jackdaws that scatters the Scarecrow's straw stuffing, afterward helping see the Scarecrow refilled with money recovered from the Jackdaws' nest.

## Relationships

**[[Nick Chopper]]** — friend. The Tin Woodman tolerates the Woggle-Bug's abrupt arrival and lengthy self-introduction ("You may say what you please," he tells him briefly), and the two seem bound afterward through shared adventures, from building the flying Thing together to fending off the Jackdaw attack.

**[[The Scarecrow]]** — friend. The Scarecrow greets the Woggle-Bug's sudden appearance with startled courtesy ("your abrupt appearance has caused me surprise"), and later praises one of his remarks as "Spoken like a philosopher!", suggesting an easy companionship between them.

**[[Tip]]** — acquaintance. Tip grows visibly provoked by the Woggle-Bug's insistence on puns, telling him "your joke is a poor one, and as old as it is poor," yet still crawls free to assist the Woggle-Bug after the Jackdaws' assault, hinting at a wary but loyal bond.

**[[Jack Pumpkinhead]]** — acquaintance. Stranded on the mountain, the Woggle-Bug laments "This is a worse prison than the palace," echoed by Jack Pumpkinhead's own fear that "the mountain air isn't good for pumpkins," suggesting shared unease between them in moments of danger.

**[[General Jinjur]]** — enemy. When the Woggle-Bug suggests she marry the Queen to settle her rebellion, Jinjur "glared at the insect fiercely," indicating open hostility between them.

## Biography

The Woggle-Bug serves as Public Accuser at the trial of Dorothy's kitten, chosen for the role because he is so learned that no one can deceive him. Addressing the jury, his tone is pompous, and he struts up and down in an absurd attempt to appear dignified. He shows a fastidious regard for order in his own thinking, curtly telling Dorothy not to interrupt him because he does not like anything upsetting his thoughts once he has them arranged.

## Relationships

**[[Princess Ozma]]** — employment. Woggle-Bug's role as Public Accuser, assigned at Ozma's signal, seems to place him in Ozma's service.

**[[DOROTHY]]** — acquaintance. Woggle-Bug's rebuke of DOROTHY during the trial ("Don't interrupt, little girl") suggests only a passing acquaintance between them.

**[[Eureka]]** — enemy. As Public Accuser prosecuting Eureka, Woggle-Bug's position could indicate an adversarial standing toward her.

**[[Scarecrow]]** — friendly_rivalry. Their connection seems to suggest a rivalry, though the nature of it is not established.

**[[WIZARD]]** — acquaintance. Their association appears to be no more than an acquaintance.

page.title: His Majesty
page.content:
## Infobox

- Name: His Majesty

## Biography

"His Majesty" is the title used to address and refer to the Scarecrow in his capacity as ruler. The Soldier with the Green Whiskers uses the title when explaining what must be done with a newly arrived visitor, telling the Guardian of the Gates, "I must take him to His Majesty, the Scarecrow," and later cutting off further questions by stating, "That is His Majesty's business." Under this title the Scarecrow receives visitors directly: upon meeting Jack, His Majesty at first suspected the visitor of laughing at him, then made a careful examination and discovered that Jack's carved features were fixed in a permanent smile. His Majesty communicates partly through gestures, asking "Did you understand that sign?", and relies on Jellia to translate for a visitor, as when she reports, "His Majesty inquires if you are hungry." His Majesty is also shown occupied with leisure and practical matters of state, throwing quoits calmly even while his throne was said to be threatened, and later inspecting a horse brought to him, judging it critically with the remark, "He doesn't seem especially graceful!"

## Events

Under this title, the Scarecrow, ruler of the Emerald City, meets Jack Pumpkinhead.

## References

page.content:
## Infobox

- Place type: Palace
- Region: Kingdom of the Winkies

## Biography

The Emperor designates the seat of the Tin Woodman (Nick Chopper), who rules over the Winkies and calls himself their Emperor, having made himself an Absolute Monarch whose conduct of public or personal affairs no one interferes with. Also referred to as the Emperor's palace, it stands within the City of the Winkies, forming part of the castle and city of the Tin Woodman, and its ruler has recently been nickel-plated.

## Events

Fearing for his safety, the Scarecrow resolves to flee to the Emperor's domain, seeking protection from his friend the Tin Woodman. Tip and the Scarecrow's party later reach the City of the Winkies and its Emperor's palace, where they are told that the Tin Woodman was made Emperor of the Winkies after the destruction of the Wicked Witch, and that the Emperor has recently been polished and had himself nickel-plated.

## Biography

The Emperor rules from a tin castle whose furniture, floors, and walls are all made of brightly polished tin, a detail he takes pride in showing visitors. He dresses only in tin himself and offers hospitality to guests, inviting them to prepare for dinner served in his grand tin dining-hall.

page.title: Emperor
page.content:
## Biography

The Emperor is nickel-plated and kept free of rust by thousands of Winkies who polish his castle out of devotion to him. His people are described as loving to do anything in their power for their beloved Emperor. He maintains a Tin Cornet Band, which entertained guests one evening with several melodies after dinner.

## Relationships

**[[Dorothy]]** — friend. Their frequent appearance together suggests a friendly bond, though the excerpts do not detail its nature.

**[[Ozma]]** — ally. Their association could indicate an alliance, though this is not explicitly confirmed.

**[[Roquat]]** — enemy. Their opposition seems suggested by context, though not explicitly stated.

**[[Wizard]]** — friend. The Wizard's familiarity with the Emperor's castle and habits suggests a friendly acquaintance.

page.content:
## Biography

The Jackdaws are a colony of birds that has built an immense nest in a hollow ledge of rock. Over the years the Jackdaws have stolen money from villages and cities, hoarding bills of various denominations along with jewels and trinkets inside their nest. When intruders fall into their territory, the Jackdaws react with jabbering and a great flopping of wings, and are considered dangerous enough that Tip warns the group they would surely be killed by the birds' anger. The Woggle-Bug identifies the Jackdaws as the greatest enemies of his race, and during the encounter the birds tear apart the Scarecrow's straw stuffing, scattering it into the chasm below.

## Relationships

**[[Nick Chopper]]** — possibly an enemy, as the Jackdaws' assault on the party while he was present suggests mutual hostility.

**[[Saw-Horse]]** — possibly an enemy, given the Jackdaws' attack on the group during the Saw-Horse's presence.

**[[The Scarecrow]]** — possibly an enemy; the Jackdaws' attack scattered the Scarecrow's stuffing into the chasm, leaving him an empty suit of clothes.

**[[Woggle-Bug]]** — possibly an enemy; the Woggle-Bug describes Jackdaws as the greatest enemies of his race.

## Infobox

## Biography

The Gump is a flying construct assembled atop the palace roof from the head of a Gump mounted with antlers, two sofas bound together as a body, and four palm-tree leaves cut by the Tin Woodman and attached as wings, held together with ropes and a broom. Once brought to life, it could speak, obey commands, and fly by waving its four wings, carrying Tip, the Scarecrow, the Tin Woodman, Jack Pumpkinhead, the Woggle-Bug, and the Saw-Horse south in search of Glinda the Good.

## Events

- Assembled on the palace roof and brought to life; obeyed Tip's command to return and landed safely.
- Carried the group south through the night toward Glinda the Good, flying beyond the Land of Oz into unfamiliar territory.
- Misjudged its landing speed, broke both right wings against a cliff edge, and tumbled down before catching on a projecting rock.
- Its nest on the cliff was attacked by jackdaws, fought off by the Tin Woodman and the Saw-Horse.
- Had its broken wings mended by the Woggle-Bug's wish, restoring full flight.

## Biography

Pastoria was the former King of the Emerald City before the Wonderful Wizard took the crown from him. According to Glinda, the throne of the Emerald City rightfully belongs to Pastoria rather than to Jinjur or the Scarecrow, since it was usurped from him by the Wizard. Pastoria is now dead, and is said to have had a daughter who is the rightful heir to the throne of the Emerald City.

page.title: Journey
page.content:
## Infobox

- Name: Journey
- Destination: Emerald City

## Biography

The Journey is the expedition undertaken toward the Emerald City, prepared in haste by the emperor, who instructed his Lord High Chancellor to run the kingdom during his absence. Once underway, the party — including the Tin Woodman and, later, the one-legged Pumpkinhead, who was perched upon the Saw-Horse and tied to his seat with cords so he could not fall off — pressed onward toward the Emerald City. Despite knowing every step of the route by heart, the Tin Woodman found that something curious had happened and feared the group had already lost its way, a disturbance caused by Mombi's secret magic, which she worked from a locked tower room to prevent the travelers' return.

page.title: Saw-Horse
page.content:
## Biography

Saw-Horse est un cheval de bois animé, capable de galoper et de parler. Sur la route menant à la Cité d'Émeraude, il file comme un cheval de course tandis que Jack Pumpkinhead se cramponne à un poteau, et les tours et dômes verts de la cité finissent par apparaître à l'horizon. Craignant le feu en raison de la sécheresse de son bois, qui selon lui s'enflammerait comme du petit bois, il manifeste une vive agitation face à ce danger. Il propose également de « secouer » une jeune fille, suggestion à laquelle le Bûcheron de Fer-Blanc répond qu'il convient au contraire de la traiter avec douceur et de la renvoyer comblée de bijoux.

## Relationships

**[[Tip]]** — other. The Saw-Horse carried Tip on its rides toward the Emerald City, though at one point it raced ahead without realizing Tip had been left behind, which could suggest their bond was more practical than deeply attentive.

**[[Jack Pumpkinhead]]** — friendly_rivalry. The two traveled together, with the Saw-Horse once turning and prancing in agitation at the mention of fire, warning that its own dry wood would burn like kindling — an exchange that suggests an easy, if occasionally tense, companionship with Jack.

**[[General Jinjur]]** — enemy. When Jinjur was found seated on the throne, the Saw-Horse suggested giving her "a good shaking," a remark the Tin Woodman rebuffed in favor of gentler treatment, hinting at an adversarial attitude toward her.

**[[Jackdaws]]** — enemy. Their shared presence in the same events could suggest a wary footing between them, though the excerpts record no direct exchange.

**[[Nick Chopper]]** — ally. Their travels together seem to place them on the same side of events, though the excerpts do not detail direct interaction between them.

## Biography

The Sawhorse is a creature encountered in the company of the Cowardly Lion, the King of the Forest and vassal of Princess Ozma, and the Hungry Tiger, the terror of the jungle. It introduces the newcomer known as the Real Horse to these two in a calm tone and with as much dignity as it can muster, bowing its head toward them. The Sawhorse openly admires the Real Horse, calling it a beautiful animal. When the Scarecrow proposes a race between the Sawhorse and the Cab-horse, the Sawhorse draws back, protesting that such a contest would not be fair.

page.content:
## Biography

The Guardian of the Gates admits visitors to the Emerald City on behalf of His Majesty, the Scarecrow. When a stranger is brought before him, he decides he must take him to the Scarecrow, deferring judgment on his fate to "His Majesty's business." Later, when General Jinjur's army threatens to conquer the city, the Guardian grows uneasy and rings the bell for the Soldier with the Green Whiskers, only to find himself surrounded by Jinjur's girls, who jab knitting-needles near his face until, howling for mercy, he offers no resistance as Jinjur takes the bunch of keys from around his neck.

## Relationships

**[[General Jinjur]]** — enemy. Jinjur's advance on the city seems to have made the Guardian uneasy, suggesting an adversarial dynamic between them.

**[[Jack Pumpkinhead]]** — acquaintance. The Guardian's decision to bring him before the Scarecrow suggests a passing acquaintance rather than any deeper bond.

**[[Soldier with the Green Whiskers]]** — acquaintance. The Guardian's habit of ringing for him suggests a working acquaintance between the two.

page.title: Jack Pumpkinhead
page.content:
## Biography

Jack Pumpkinhead, also called Jack or Pumpkinhead, is a man built from wood and topped with a carved pumpkin for a head. He was fashioned by Tip, who afterward maintained that "Jack belongs to me, for I made him even if the old witch did bring him to life" — the witch in question being old Mombi, who animated him by means of a magical powder kept in an old pepper-box. He received his name when a companion declared, "I believe I will name the fellow 'Jack Pumpkinhead!'"

Jack's body is stiff and poorly suited to ordinary movement. His joints are weak, and when he first tried to walk he had to be dragged and pushed into motion, tumbling several times before he could manage the bend in the road on his own. Sitting is especially hazardous to him: on one occasion he attempted to rest on an old sawhorse, and as soon as he bent his joints further than usual they gave way entirely, sending him crashing to the ground. After this he was advised, "I guess you'd better remain standing, hereafter. It seems the safest way."

Jack does not share ordinary human needs. When invited to breakfast, he declined to join in, explaining, "I don't seem to be made the same way you are."

On the road to the Emerald City, Jack presented himself to the Guardian of the Gates, who asked who he was and what his business might be. Jack answered plainly, "My name is Jack Pumpkinhead, but as to my business, I haven't the least idea in the world what it is," an answer that left the Guardian visibly dissatisfied.

At a river crossing, a ferryman refused passage and dismissed him as a "pumpkinheaded loon," indifferent to whether he sank or swam. Undisturbed, Jack replied, "Don't worry about me, I'm sure I ought to float beautifully," and waded in himself, holding the tail of the Saw-Horse to keep his pumpkin head above the water while the party crossed.

## Narrative role

Jack Pumpkinhead — also known simply as Jack or Pumpkinhead — began his existence as a carved wooden figure fashioned by Tip. After building the body and fitting it with a pumpkin head, Tip dressed the finished figure in clothes taken from Old Mombi's chest and gave it the name "Jack Pumpkinhead."

As Jack and Tip set out together, Jack grew anxious that his wooden joints would wear out from walking. When he attempted to sit down on an old sawhorse resting at the edge of a wood, his joints gave way entirely and he collapsed; Tip lifted him back to his feet and advised him to remain standing from then on. The pair debated whether the sawhorse truly resembled a real horse, weighing its tree-trunk body, branch tail, knot eyes, and carved mouth, and Jack observed that since he himself was made of wood yet alive, the sawhorse might likewise be brought to life.

In the Emerald City, Jack admitted his mistake in assuming that an interpreter would be needed. The Scarecrow then declared the two of them friends and led Jack off to play quoits. Jack Pumpkinhead's meeting with His Majesty the Scarecrow, ruler of the Emerald City, is also recorded, along with a shared discovery that only one language was spoken throughout Oz.

Later, while crossing a river, Jack's pumpkin head was swept downstream; Tip retrieved it with a long pole and reattached it to his neck, after which Jack worried anxiously that water or sunshine might spoil or crack it. The group then remounted the Saw-Horse and resumed traveling toward Nick Chopper, with Jack and the horse bickering along the way. Upon arrival, Nick Chopper welcomed Tip, Jack Pumpkinhead, and the Saw-Horse, and explained that the engraved star on his chest covered the patch where the Wizard of Oz had placed his heart.

The group later escaped a field of sunflowers by riding forward with their eyes closed, following the lead of the Pumpkinhead and the Saw-Horse. Afterward, Nick Chopper amputated Jack's damaged left leg and fitted it to the Saw-Horse, an exchange that prompted further bickering between Jack and the horse before the group resumed its travel toward the Emerald City.

Nick Chopper subsequently repaired Jack's broken leg with a table leg, and the group dispersed to gather materials for an aerial machine; palm leaves were fastened as wings, and Jack's broom was added as a tail for steering. The finished craft, the Gump, then flew south carrying Tip, the Scarecrow, Nick Chopper, Jack Pumpkinhead, the Woggle-Bug, and the Saw-Horse aboard.

## Personality

Jack shows an amiable, unguarded temperament, meeting even his own uncertain nature with equanimity rather than distress: asked by the Guardian of the Gates about his business, he answers, smilingly, that he has "not the least idea in the world what it is," untroubled by not knowing. The same good humor surfaces when a hostile ferryman dismisses him outright — Jack answers with a smile that he expects to "float beautifully," an unshaken cheerfulness even when others treat him with contempt or indifference.

His curiosity runs outward more than inward: he watches Tip "curiously" over breakfast, remarking only that he is "not made the same way" rather than pressing the matter, and later offers Tip the practical suggestion of carving ears for the Saw-Horse so it might be told what to do — a small but concrete instance of problem-solving. Beneath this composure runs a current of physical anxiety tied to his fragile condition: he asks, fearfully, whether fire is dangerous to pumpkins, a rare admission of worry set against his usual even temper.

## Appearance

Jack Pumpkinhead is built with a carved pumpkin for a head, the detail behind the name given him at his creation. His frame is heavy and awkward to move, needing to be dragged and walked into position by bending one leg's joints, then the other, while being pushed from behind.

His joints are notably weak: bending them further than usual makes them give way entirely, and he comes clattering to the ground, after which his arms and legs must be straightened and his head checked for cracks. Because of this fragility, remaining standing rather than sitting is judged the safer posture for him. When wading through water, he must keep his pumpkin head lifted above the surface to keep it from harm.

## Powers

Jack Pumpkinhead owes his very existence to magic: he was carved from wood and a pumpkin, then brought to life by a magical powder kept in an old pepper-box. This origin leaves him fundamentally unlike an ordinary person — he does not eat, telling Tip plainly, "I don't seem to be made the same way you are," and declining to join him at breakfast.

His wooden, jointed frame is both a strength and a liability. The joints allow him to walk and stand once set in motion, but they are weak and prone to giving way entirely under strain, as when he tried to sit and collapsed in a clattering heap. When faced with crossing a river, Jack showed no fear of the water, confidently telling the ferryman, "I'm sure I ought to float beautifully" — a buoyancy his pumpkin-and-wood body would be expected to have, though only he voiced this expectation.

## Relationships

**[[Tip]]** — family. Tip carved Jack Pumpkinhead's body and brought him to life with the Powder of Life, later insisting "Jack belongs to me, for I made him even if the old witch did bring him to life"; the bond seems to carry an almost paternal weight, as Jack is said to have addressed Tip as "dear father."

**[[Nick Chopper]]** — acquaintance. In the Tin Woodman's company, Jack seems to have been accepted as a kindred figure, told "you are certainly unusual, and therefore worthy to become a member of our select society," suggesting an easy welcome among fellow unusual beings.

**[[Saw-Horse]]** — friendly_rivalry. Their bond seems built more on shared mishap than rivalry: after wading and swimming together across a river, the Saw-Horse remarked "I didn't mind swimming, at all," to which Jack answered, "Nor did I."

**[[The Scarecrow]]** — friend. Their rapport appears to rest on a mutual understanding of what it means to be a made, not born, creature, captured in an exchange noting "there is this difference between us, that whereas I will bend, but not break, you will break, but not bend."

**[[Woggle-Bug]]** — acquaintance. Their exchanges suggest quiet agreement rather than closeness, as when Jack simply acknowledged, "That is true."

## Trivia

- The name "Jack Pumpkinhead" was chosen for him on the spot by his creator, who settled on it "after a moment's thought."
- He does not eat: when invited to share a meal, he explained, "I don't seem to be made the same way you are."
- It was Jack's own idea to fashion ears for the newly animated Saw-Horse, reasoning that ears would let it be told what to do.
- Facing a river crossing with no boat available, he showed no fear of sinking, remarking that he was sure he "ought to float beautifully."

page.title: Jack Pumpkinhead
page.content:
## Biography

Jack Pumpkinhead, also known simply as Jack, is associated with a private graveyard, described as such by the Tin Woodman when Dorothy comes upon it. The graveyard holds tombstones marking not death but recurring spoilage: one reads "Here Lies the Mortal Part of JACK PUMPKINHEAD Which Spoiled April 9th," a second reads "Here Lies the Mortal Part of JACK PUMPKINHEAD Which Spoiled October 2nd," and a third reads "Here Lies the Mortal Part of JACK PUMPKINHEAD Which Spoiled January 24th."

The existence of these markers puzzles Dorothy, who remarks that she thought nobody ever died in Oz — a reaction that underscores how unusual it is for Jack to have a graveyard of his own despite still being present and, as the tombstones themselves show, having outlasted each recorded spoiling of his "mortal part."

## Narrative role

Jack Pumpkinhead is first encountered when Dorothy and her companions stop at his pumpkin farm along the road, where Nick Chopper, the Tin Woodman, recounts the story of the Powder of Life that had first brought Jack to life. During the visit, Dorothy comes upon a small graveyard on the property and asks what it is; the Tin Woodman explains it is Jack Pumpkinhead's own private graveyard. Puzzled, since she believed no one ever died in Oz, Dorothy reads the tombstones herself. Each one marks not a death but a spoiling: one records that the mortal part of Jack Pumpkinhead spoiled on April 9th, a second on October 2nd, and a third on January 24th, showing that Jack has already gone through several pumpkin heads before the one he currently wears.

## Personality

Jack Pumpkinhead's face is described as jolly and smiling, a bearing that drew Button-Bright to grow fond of him.

The Tin Woodman's readiness to fetch Dorothy to Jack's house upon learning he is "still alive" suggests Jack is held in genuine affection by his companions, despite the fragile, ever-spoiling nature of his pumpkin head.

## Appearance

Jack Pumpkinhead's defining physical trait is named directly: his head is carved from a pumpkin, and this head constitutes what is called his "mortal part." This mortal part decays over time — tombstones in his private graveyard record that it "spoiled" on three separate occasions, dated April 9th, October 2nd, and January 24th, indicating that his pumpkin head has been replaced more than once.

## Powers

Jack Pumpkinhead does not perish in the ordinary sense. Behind his home lies a private graveyard holding no bodies, only small tombstones marking when a previous pumpkin head "spoiled" — first on April 9th, then October 2nd, then January 24th. Since nobody is ever said to truly die in Oz, this suggests that the spoiling of a pumpkin head ends only that "mortal part" of Jack rather than Jack himself, hinting at a capacity to continue on beyond the loss of any single head.

## Relationships

**[[Dorothy]]** — friend. Their bond seems close, as Dorothy sighs "Poor Jack! I'm sorry he had to die in three parts," suggesting genuine concern for Jack's periodic spoiling.

**[[Nick Chopper]]** — friend. The Tin Woodman's declaration, "So you shall, since he is still alive. Come with me to his house," suggests a welcoming, supportive bond toward Jack.

**[[Ozma]]** — family. Jack's own words, "Ozma's my parent, you know, because she built my body and carved my pumpkin head," suggest he regards her as a parental figure owing to her role in his creation.

**[[Button-Bright]]** — friend. The boy's fondness seems to stem from Jack's demeanor, as "Jack's face was so jolly and smiling that the boy soon grew to like him."

## Trivia

- Jack Pumpkinhead maintains a private graveyard containing the remains of his previous pumpkin heads once they spoiled.
- Three graves are recorded there, marking heads that spoiled on April 9th, October 2nd, and January 24th.
- Dorothy initially believed nobody in Oz ever died, making the discovery of Jack's graveyard a surprise to her.
- Despite the graves marking his spoiled heads, Jack Pumpkinhead is still alive, as Nick Chopper confirms when referring to him as "still alive."

## Biography

Jack Pumpkinhead is a farmer whose farm consists of a vast pumpkin field, where some of the pumpkins grow to enormous size. He designed his own house, which stands not far from the Scarecrow's mansion. Like the Scarecrow, the Tin Woodman, and Tiktok, he has no need to sleep. He counts the Tin Woodman and the Scarecrow among his companions, and, together with the Tin Woodman and the Shaggy Man, he declared his intention to stand by Ozma.

## Relationships

**[[Scarecrow]]** — friend. Jack Pumpkinhead is named alongside the Scarecrow as one of the Wizard's old friends, and the two are described waiting out a night together at the Forbidden Fountain, suggesting a close bond.

**[[Ozma]]** — friend. Jack Pumpkinhead's declaration that he would stand by Ozma suggests loyalty toward her.

**[[Nick Chopper]]** — friend. His presence alongside the Tin Woodman during a visit to the tin castle suggests a friendly acquaintance.

**[[Tiktok]]** — friend. His overnight vigil beside the Forbidden Fountain alongside Tiktok suggests a companionable relationship.

page.title: Old Mombi
page.content:
## Biography

Old Mombi, known simply as Mombi, is an old woman living in the Country of the Gillikins in the North of the Land of Oz, where she serves as guardian to the boy Tip, raising him since early childhood though he remembers nothing of his parents. Her reputation is poor: the Gillikin people suspect her of practicing magical arts and largely avoid her company. Because the ruling Good Witch has forbidden any other Witch to exist within her dominion, Mombi cannot claim that title outright and is restricted to working as a Sorceress, or at most a Wizardess. She actively pursues magical knowledge, at one point trading secrets with a crooked wizard living in a mountain cave in exchange for three recipes, four magical powders, and a selection of potent herbs, and she keeps a pepper-box containing the Powder of Life among her possessions.

When Tip flees her household after fashioning and animating a pumpkin-headed man named Jack, Mombi discovers the trick and grows furious, both at the deception and at the theft of the Powder of Life. Later, General Jinjur summons her to the Emerald City to help repel the returning Scarecrow and Tin Woodman, and from a tower room she works magic to disorient the travelers, at one point sending a sheet of crackling flame across the meadow toward them. Her history with magic runs deeper still: Glinda later argues that the Wizard of Oz must have taught Mombi many of his tricks in exchange for some earlier assistance, and suspects — though does not confirm — that Mombi helped him conceal the girl Ozma, the rightful heir to the throne of the Emerald City, prompting Glinda to seek Mombi out to force her to reveal where the girl is hidden.

## Relationships

**[[Glinda the Good]]** — enemy. Glinda vows to march on the Emerald City to "take Mombi prisoner," suggesting the two stand as opposed forces.

**[[General Jinjur]]** — wary alliance. Jinjur sends for Mombi and promises her rewards for aid against the Scarecrow and Tin Woodman, an alliance that seems born of convenience rather than trust.

**[[Tip]]** — enemy. Mombi's fury at Tip's trick and his theft of the Powder of Life points to a bond turned to enmity after his escape.

**[[The Scarecrow]]** — enemy. Mombi's magical assaults against the traveling party, which included the Scarecrow, suggest she counted him among her foes.

**[[Wizard of Oz]]** — wary alliance. Glinda's account that "the Wizard taught the old woman many of his tricks of magic" hints at a past working arrangement between the two, offered only as suspicion.

page.title: Mombi
page.content:
## Biography

Mombi est une Sorcière malfaisante qui régna autrefois sur le Nord du pays d'Oz, à l'époque où quatre Sorcières se partageaient le royaume. Elle enleva le grand-père d'Ozma, alors souverain, pendant une partie de chasse, et le retint prisonnier, agissant ensuite comme geôlière du père d'Ozma après lui. Elle fut finalement vaincue dans le Nord par une Sorcière bienfaisante. C'est également Mombi qui, à la naissance d'Ozma, la transforma en garçon, espérant ainsi empêcher quiconque de reconnaître en elle la véritable princesse du pays d'Oz.

## Biography

Mombi is a Witch who obtained the Powder of Life from a crooked Sorcerer living in the mountains of the North Country and brought it home with her. Before Ozma became Princess of Oz, Ozma lived with Mombi, who had transformed her into the shape of a boy. While Mombi was away visiting the crooked Sorcerer, the boy fashioned a pumpkin-headed man, partly to amuse himself and partly hoping to frighten Mombi upon her return. Mombi was not frightened by the creation; instead, she sprinkled the Pumpkinhead with her Magic Powder of Life to see whether it would work.

page.content:
## Biography

General Jinjur is the commander of the Army of Revolt, a force she assembled from all parts of the Land of Oz — Munchkin, Quadling, Winkie, and Gillikin recruits, each company distinguished by a different colored strip on their uniforms — marching at her express command against the Emerald City. Having taken the city, she moves from military commander to self-declared monarch: she is found seated on the Scarecrow's throne, wearing his second-best crown and holding the royal sceptre, eating caramels, and she declares that "the throne belongs to whoever is able to take it" and that she is now Queen, with anyone who opposes her guilty of treason. Fearing that the Scarecrow and the Tin Woodman might join forces against her, she sends for the witch Old Mombi, offering her large rewards to prevent their return to the Emerald City.

## Relationships

**[[The Scarecrow]]** — enemy. Jinjur's unease over the Scarecrow's escape from the Emerald City, and their later confrontation in the throne room where he challenges her right to sit on his throne, suggest a rivalry between the two rulers.

**[[Old Mombi]]** — wary alliance. Jinjur summoned Mombi and promised her large rewards to help defend the rebel army against the Scarecrow and the Tin Woodman, suggesting a tactical alliance forged out of shared need rather than trust.

**[[Glinda the Good]]** — enemy. Evidence tied to Jinjur's demand that Mombi be delivered up as a prisoner could indicate an antagonistic stance toward Glinda.

**[[Jack Pumpkinhead]]** — enemy. Jack's fear of being turned into tarts or soup at Jinjur's hands points to an adversarial dynamic, though this reflects his own apprehension rather than a confirmed fact.

**[[Nick Chopper]]** — enemy. Nick Chopper's remark that "Jinjur is still the Queen, and we are her prisoners" reflects the captor role she held over him and his companions.

page.content:
## Biography

Jinjur is a dairy-maid encountered along the road, recognized by Ozma despite her humble occupation and greeting her with a curtsy as "your Highness." She had previously assembled an army of women, driven the Scarecrow from the throne of the Emerald City, and fought a battle against the powerful army of Glinda the Sorceress. By the time of this encounter, she has married a man who owns nine cows and describes herself as happy, contented, and willing to lead a quiet life, minding her own business.

## Relationships

**[[Glinda the Good]]** — enemy. Jinjur once fought a battle against Glinda's army, which could indicate a lasting rivalry between them.

**[[Ozma]]** — acquaintance. Ozma recognizes Jinjur on sight as a dairy-maid, suggesting the two are already familiar with one another.

**[[Scarecrow]]** — enemy. Jinjur once drove the Scarecrow from the throne of the Emerald City, suggesting an adversarial history between them.

page.title: General Guph
page.content:
## Biography

General Guph, referred to at times simply as the General or the Captain General, holds the rank of General. He is recorded returning to the cavern of the Nome King, where the King greets him with "Well, what luck? Will the Whimsies join us?" Guph answers, "They will," a reply that indicates he had been dealing with the Whimsies on the King's behalf and came back with a favorable answer.

In the company of Dorothy, the Wizard, the Shaggy Man, and the Tin Woodman, the Captain General takes part in a journey through Oz. He asks where the group is to go next, noting that "we haven't visited the Rigmaroles or the Flutterbudgets yet," and remarks that he is "glad we visited the Fuddles." Later, as the party crosses from the Gillikin Country into the Country of the Winkies, he calls out to note the change from purple to yellow hues, saying, "Aha! here is the Country of the Winkies. We are just crossing the boundary line."

During this same journey, the Captain General speaks favorably of the Wizard, telling Dorothy that "all the people of Oz...are very proud of their Wizard," and recalling that "he once made some soap-bubbles that astonished the world." He also asks whether the Scarecrow has heard of Ozma's trouble, a question the Wizard answers in the negative.

## Personality

General Guph presents himself as confident and assured of his own effectiveness. Reporting to the Nome King on his recruiting efforts, he answers plainly and without hesitation — "They will," and "Yes, indeed... I have their promise" — a directness that contrasts with the King's disbelief ("No!" cried the astonished King) and suggests Guph trusts his own success even when his superior does not share that confidence.

Among Dorothy's traveling companions, where he is addressed as the Captain General, Guph shows a more inquisitive and appreciative side. He asks where the party will travel next ("Where to?") and, as concern grows over Ozma's situation, presses for news of the Scarecrow ("Has the Scarecrow heard of Ozma's trouble?"), showing attentiveness to the group's unfolding troubles. He also voices open admiration for the Wizard, describing him as someone "all the people of Oz" take pride in, and expresses simple contentment with the day's outing ("For my part, I'm glad we visited the Fuddles.").

## Relationships

**[[Roquat]]** — employment. When General Guph returned to the cavern of the Nome King, his Majesty asked, "Well, what luck? Will the Whimsies join us?" — an exchange that suggests Guph serves the Nome King in a subordinate, employed capacity.

**[[King]]** — employment. A further exchange, "Very well, your Majesty. Do what you will with the girls for all I care," again seems to place Guph in service to a king, reporting outcomes and deferring to royal authority.

**[[Dorothy]]** — acquaintance. Guph, addressed here as the Captain General, is present when Dorothy and her companions discuss their travels — "What! Are we going to Fuddlecumjig?" asked the Captain General — suggesting at least a passing acquaintance between them.

**[[Nick Chopper]]** — acquaintance. In conversation the Captain General asks, "Has the Scarecrow heard of Ozma's trouble?" of the Tin Woodman, indicating a similarly casual, acquainted rapport.

**[[Ozma]]** — enemy. A note attributed to Guph, "Ozma is surely lost," could indicate an adversarial stance toward Ozma, though the phrasing alone offers only a tentative basis for this reading.

## Trivia

- Addressed as "Captain General" while traveling with Dorothy's companions, but simply as "General" or "Guph" when reporting to the Nome King.
- Traveled through Fuddlecumjig and the Country of the Winkies alongside Dorothy, the Wizard, the Shaggy Man, and the Tin Woodman.
- Returned to the cavern of the Nome King specifically to report on whether the Whimsies would join, answering "They will" when asked.
- Spoke proudly of the Wizard, noting that "all the people of Oz are very proud of their Wizard" and recalling that "he once made some soap-bubbles that astonished the world."

page.title: Ozma
page.content:
## Biography

Ozma is the Ruler of Oz, referred to as "the girlish Ruler of Oz." She presides over her court from the palace, seating her guests — including Tiktok, the Scarecrow, and the Tin Woodman — and directing state affairs. In one such gathering she calls a solemn conference to decide how to liberate the royal family of the Land of Ev from their long imprisonment, and she directly challenges the King's claim to have rightfully purchased that family as slaves, telling him plainly, "But that was wrong."

According to Dorothy's account, Ozma leads an expedition of Dorothy, the Scarecrow, the Tin Woodman, Tiktok, Billina, the Cowardly Lion, and the army of Oz to free the Queen of Ev and her ten children from the Nome King, traveling to his underground palace. There the Nome King challenges Ozma to identify the enchanted royal family among his ornaments within eleven guesses, or become an ornament herself. After the royal family's recovery and the crowning of Evardo Fifteenth as King of Ev, Dorothy accepts Ozma's invitation to return with her to the Land of Oz.

## Relationships

**[[Dorothy]]** — friend. Their exchange in council — "We shall do it" — seems to reflect a shared resolve between the two, as Ozma keeps a chair at her own side for Dorothy during the conference on Ev.

**[[Nome King]]** — enemy. Ozma's flat rebuke of his claim that "the king can do no wrong" for enslaving the royal family of Ev — "But that was wrong" — suggests an adversarial relationship between them.

**[[Tin Woodman]]** — employment. He describes himself as acting on her command, "our gracious Ruler ordered me to assemble our army, which I did," indicating her authority over him.

**[[Scarecrow]]** — friend. He is seated near her council table at the palace, among those gathered around her for the conference on Ev, which seems to place him within her close circle.

**[[King]]** — enemy. The King who insists he lawfully purchased the royal family of Ev as slaves is met with Ozma's rebuke, "But that was wrong," pointing to an antagonistic relationship.

contributions.title: Dorothy and the Wizard in Oz

page.title: Princess Ozma
page.content:
## Biography

Princess Ozma is the ruler of the Land of Oz. She presides in her court from a magnificent emerald throne, holding a jewelled sceptre and wearing a sparkling coronet, with the twenty-eight officers of her army and officials of the royal household standing behind her.

Ozma possesses the Nome King's Magic Belt and an enchanted picture through which she watches distant events. She has promised to look into the picture each day at four o'clock, and if she sees a certain sign, she will put on the Belt and wish the sender to be brought to her in Oz.

Ozma once brought the Sawhorse to life with a witch-powder, said to have been a boy at that time. After the Sawhorse won a race, she took the coronet from her own head and set it upon the horse, proclaiming him Prince of Horses and declaring that all other horses in the Land of Oz must thereafter be considered imitations of him.

When Dorothy reaches the palace, she is kept in Ozma's private rooms, and Jellia Jamb welcomes Zeb on Ozma's orders. Ozma also summons Eureka the kitten to speak with her directly, and later presides over a crowded public trial in the Throne Room, dressed in her most splendid robes of state.

## Narrative role

Princess Ozma rules from the Emerald City and keeps watch over the Land of Oz through her enchanted picture, which she consults every day at four o'clock. When Dorothy makes the agreed sign, Ozma puts on the Nome King's Magic Belt and wishes Dorothy, and then the rest of Dorothy's companions, to her side in the Emerald City.

Once the travelers arrive at the palace, a race is run between Jim and the Sawhorse. After the Sawhorse wins, injuring a leg and an ear in the contest, the Tin Woodman repairs the damage with a fresh limb cut from a tree. Ozma then takes the coronet from her own head and sets it upon the Sawhorse, proclaiming it Prince of Horses and declaring that, in the Land of Oz at least, every other horse must henceforth be considered a mere imitation of the Sawhorse.

Some time afterward, one of Ozma's white piglets disappears from her boudoir, and Dorothy's kitten Eureka is seen fleeing the room.

Ozma holds Eureka responsible for the piglet's disappearance, treating it as a killing, and orders the kitten imprisoned and brought to trial for murder before a jury of nine.

## Personality

Ozma shows herself as attentive and protective toward those she considers friends: she arranges to watch over Dorothy through an enchanted picture at a fixed hour each day, ready to invoke the Nome King's Magic Belt the moment a sign of distress appears. This routine suggests a ruler who takes personal responsibility for the safety of her companions rather than delegating it.

Her conduct at court reveals a gracious and ceremonious disposition. After the race between Jim and the Sawhorse, she publicly rewards the winner with her own coronet and a formal proclamation naming him "Prince of Horses," a gesture that shows generosity toward merit and a taste for solemn ritual. The same formality marks her appearance at the trial in the Throne Room, where she presides in her most splendid robes of state, sceptre and coronet in place, before a full court of officers and officials.

Ozma's interest in the Wizard, described as curiosity to meet a man of his renown, hints — though only tentatively — at an inquisitive streak toward figures of unusual reputation.

## Appearance

During the trial held in the Throne Room, Ozma appeared dressed in her most splendid robes of state, her jewelled sceptre in hand and a sparkling coronet upon her fair brow. This same coronet later left her own head when she placed it upon the Sawhorse's, honoring the wooden creature's victory in the race.

## Powers

Ozma keeps an enchanted picture in which she can watch distant events; each day at a fixed hour she looks into it to see whether anyone in need has made a sign calling for her help. She also holds the Nome King's Magic Belt, which she can put on to draw a person to her side in the Land of Oz at will. Her command of magic reaches back to a time when she was still a boy: using a witch-powder, she brought the Sawhorse to life.

## Relationships

**[[DOROTHY]]** — amitié. Ozma est désignée comme « mon amie la princesse Ozma », ce qui suggère un lien amical entre les deux.

**[[Woggle-Bug]]** — autorité. Lors du procès, c'est à un signal d'Ozma que le Woggle-Bug s'adresse au jury, ce qui pourrait indiquer une relation d'autorité de la princesse envers lui.

**[[Zeb]]** — attirance naissante. Le garçon aurait laissé échapper un soupir d'admiration en sa présence, ce qui pourrait suggérer un début d'attirance, sans certitude.

**[[WIZARD]]** — connaissance. Ozma se serait montrée curieuse de rencontrer le célèbre Magicien, ce qui suggère une relation de simple connaissance entre eux.

**[[Sawhorse]]** — amitié. Le Sawhorse évoque des aventures partagées avec Ozma et affirme qu'elle l'apprécie, ce qui indique une relation amicale entre eux.

## Trivia

- Ozma keeps an enchanted picture in which she can see distant places; by arrangement with Dorothy, she looks into it every day at four o'clock, and if Dorothy makes a certain sign, Ozma dons the Nome King's Magic Belt and wishes her back to the Land of Oz.
- According to an account given to Zeb, Ozma once brought the Sawhorse to life with a witch-powder "when she was a boy," a remark that left Zeb wondering aloud whether Ozma had once been male.
- During the Throne Room trial, Ozma presided in her most splendid robes of state, bearing a jewelled sceptre and a sparkling coronet, with twenty-eight officers of her army standing behind her throne.

page.title: Ozma
page.content:
## Biography

Ozma, also called Princess Ozma, rules the Emerald City and all four countries of Oz. Each of those countries has its own lesser ruler; by the shaggy man's account, confirmed by the boy at his side, these local rulers stand beneath Ozma much as officers stand beneath a general, with Ozma holding the highest position among them.

Ozma commands magic beyond her rank. She has brought Dorothy over to Oz on her Magic Carpet, one of the means, alongside the Nome King's Magic Belt, by which Dorothy has reached the Emerald City.

## Narrative role

Ozma's part in the story centers on her authority as ruler of Oz. The Cowardly Lion and the Hungry Tiger meet the traveling party with Ozma's golden chariot and escort them into the Emerald City and into the royal palace. Later, Ozma's birthday celebration draws many guests to the palace and its grounds; once the festivities end, the [[Wizard]] sends several of the visitors home in magic bubbles, while Dorothy returns to Kansas by the Magic Belt.

## Personality

Ozma's authority is described as comprehensive yet layered: she "rules the Emerald City and all the four countries of Oz," while each country retains its own lesser ruler beneath her — an arrangement likened to an army, where "the little rulers are all captains, and Ozma's the general." This framing casts her as a sovereign who holds overall command without displacing the local governance beneath her, suggesting a disposition toward structured, delegated rule rather than direct micromanagement of every territory.

Consistent with this standing, she is said to have welcomed a visitor to Oz "in gracious accents" as "the girl Ruler" — a detail suggesting a courteous, dignified bearing toward those entering her domain, in keeping with her position as its foremost authority.

## Powers

Ozma commands magic beyond her own person: her Magic Carpet can carry a traveler across vast distances in an instant, as when it brought a companion back to the Emerald City after other magic had failed. Her authority extends over the Emerald City and all four countries of Oz, each governed by a lesser ruler who answers to her — as captains answer to a general.

## Relationships

**[[Dorothy]]** — friend. Dorothy recalls that "Ozma took me over on her Magic Carpet," suggesting a bond of trust and assistance between the two.

**[[Jellia Jamb]]** — employment. Jellia Jamb is described as "Ozma's favorite attendant," which could indicate a relationship of service within Ozma's household.

**[[Santa Claus]]** — friend. An account holds that "Ozma invited me and I just couldn't help coming to celebrate the happy occasion," hinting at a friendly rapport extending an invitation from Ozma.

**[[Jack Pumpkinhead]]** — family. Jack Pumpkinhead states, "Ozma's my parent, you know, because she built my body and carved my pumpkin head," a claim that suggests a parental bond, though it rests on Jack Pumpkinhead's own framing of his creation.

**[[THE shaggy man]]** — acquaintance. Ozma greets him with "You are welcome to Oz," spoken "in gracious accents," suggesting a cordial but formal acquaintance befitting her position as ruler.

## Trivia

- Ozma once carried Dorothy across on her Magic Carpet, one of several magical means — alongside the Silver Shoes and the Nome King's Magic Belt — that have moved Dorothy between worlds.
- Although Ozma rules the Emerald City and all four countries of Oz, each country keeps its own smaller ruler; the shaggy man compares this arrangement to a military hierarchy, with the four rulers as captains and Ozma as the general.

page.content:
## Biography

Ozma rules over all the countries of Oz, a wider authority than local rulers such as the Tin Woodman, who governs only the Winkie Country as its Emperor but answers to her. She has established what are known as the Defensive Settlements of Oz, including a town set aside for people who become Flutterbudgets, giving them a place entirely their own. She takes an interest in the excursions of her companions, having thought they might enjoy visiting the Fuddles and suggesting the trip to Fuddlecumjig. According to Dorothy, the Tin Woodman used to live with Ozma in the Emerald City before wanting a home of his own. According to the Tin Woodman's account, Ozma is said to have observed in her Magic Picture that the Nome King had dug a tunnel beneath the desert, seemingly planning an invasion of Oz alongside the Whimsies, Growleywogs, and Phanfasms.

## Relationships

**[[Dorothy]]** — friend. Ozma appears to have arranged the day's outing, having "'vised" the group to see the Rigmaroles next, suggesting a familiar, guiding friendship between the two.

**[[Roquat]]** — enemy. Ozma once forced the old Nome King to liberate his captives, an act that casts her as Roquat's adversary.

**[[Scarecrow]]** — friend. Ozma gave him land of his own, and others helped him build his mansion there, suggesting a supportive friendship.

**[[Uncle Henry]]** — employment. Some connection between them seems to exist, though the excerpts do not detail its nature.

**[[Glinda the Good]]** — ally. The two seem to share some cooperative bond, though the excerpts do not specify how.

page.title: Soldier with the Green Whiskers
page.content:
## Biography

The Soldier with the Green Whiskers, also known simply as the Soldier, is the sole soldier of the Emerald City and is himself referred to as the Royal Army of Oz. He guards the City's gates and palace, escorting visitors such as Jack Pumpkinhead into the presence of the Scarecrow and searching, on the Scarecrow's orders, for someone who understands the language of the Gillikins. When General Jinjur leads an army of girls armed with knitting-needles to conquer the Emerald City, he is summoned to the gate, confronted and overwhelmed by the attackers, and flees—without his hat or gun—to warn the Scarecrow that the City has fallen.

## Relationships

**[[The Scarecrow]]** — employment. The Soldier with the Green Whiskers carries out orders from The Scarecrow, escorting visitors to the palace and searching out an interpreter at his command, which suggests a position in his service.

**[[General Jinjur]]** — enemy. Confronted at the gateway by General Jinjur's Army, the Soldier stands against her forces before being overwhelmed, suggesting an adversarial relation between the two.

**[[Guardian]]** — acquaintance. The Soldier is summoned by the Guardian of the Gates during the standoff with Jinjur's Army, suggesting some working association between them.

**[[Jack Pumpkinhead]]** — acquaintance. The Soldier escorts Jack Pumpkinhead into the palace to see the Scarecrow, suggesting a brief acquaintance formed through that duty.

page.content:
## Biography

Jellia Jamb, also known as Jellia, is a green-clad maiden of the Emerald City who serves the Scarecrow during his reign, dismissed alongside the Soldier with the Green Whiskers after an audience and called upon to translate the Scarecrow's speech for Jack Pumpkinhead. Later, when Jinjur holds power, Mombi uses a magical rite to transform Jellia into her own likeness, taking Jellia's true form for herself so that Jellia, appearing as an aged Mombi, is led from the city gates and brought before Glinda; Glinda subsequently reverses the enchantment, restoring Jellia to her proper shape while the real Mombi resumes her own crooked form elsewhere, and the Scarecrow recognizes her again as one of his old friends.

## Relationships

**[[Jack Pumpkinhead]]** — acquaintance. Jellia's appearances alongside Jack Pumpkinhead suggest a passing acquaintance, though no direct exchange between the two is recorded.

**[[The Scarecrow]]** — employment. Jellia's presence at the Scarecrow's court, where she is called on to translate for him, could indicate a position in his service.

**[[Glinda the Good]]** — ally. Jellia's delivery before Glinda as "the person you demanded" hints at a connection between them, though the nature of any alliance is not made explicit.

**[[Old Mombi]]** — other. Mombi's use of magic to exchange forms with Jellia ties the two together, though the exact nature of their bond is not otherwise defined.

page.title: Jellia Jamb
page.content:
## Biography

Jellia Jamb is a green-robed maiden who serves as maid to Princess Ozma in the Emerald City. When the Wizard first sees her again, he greets her warmly, calling her "little Jellia Jamb" and remarking she is "as pert and pretty as ever," which suggests the two knew each other before the Princess came to rule. Jellia herself acknowledges this past but tells the Wizard he cannot rule the Emerald City as he once did, since the Emerald City now has a Princess whom everyone loves dearly.

When Zeb and the Wizard arrive at the palace, Jellia tells them that Dorothy is with Princess Ozma in the private rooms of the palace, and says Ozma has ordered her to welcome the newcomers and show them to their apartments. She is momentarily perplexed by the unfamiliar sight of the cab-horse, an animal unknown in the Land, though she decides not to be afraid of it after noting the mild look in its eyes.

As Ozma's maid, Jellia is sent to the Princess's boudoir to fetch a white piglet, but returns with a troubled face to report that the piglet is not there. Asked next to fetch Dorothy's kitten, she goes and comes back again, reporting that the kitten will not come.

## Relationships

**[[WIZARD]]** — friend. The Wizard greets her with evident familiarity and fondness, calling her "little Jellia Jamb—as pert and pretty as ever," which suggests a friendly acquaintance predating his return.

**[[Jim]]** — acquaintance. Jellia is the one who must decide how to handle Jim, the unfamiliar cab-horse brought into the palace, though her caution gives way to acceptance once she studies his manner.

**[[Princess]]** — employment. Jellia serves the Princess directly, as shown when she is sent to fetch a white piglet from the boudoir and later to retrieve Dorothy's kitten.

**[[Princess Ozma]]** — employment. Jellia's role as palace attendant appears bound to Ozma's household, though the excerpts do not detail further direct exchanges between them.

## Biography

Jellia Jamb is a pretty little maid with dark hair and eyes, dressed in green embroidered with silver. She greets Dorothy warmly upon her arrival, with Dorothy exclaiming in evident pleasure, "O Jellia Jamb! I'm so glad to see you again," suggesting the two are already well acquainted. Jellia Jamb welcomes the travelers and tells them, "Come in, please; it shall be our pleasant duty to escort all of you to the rooms prepared for your use," indicating she plays a hosting role for arriving guests. Her position could suggest a connection to Ozma, though this is not stated outright.

## Relationships

**[[Ozma]]** — employment. Jellia Jamb seems to have served in Ozma's household, described as "Ozma's favorite attendant."

**[[Dorothy]]** — friend. The two appear to share a warm, familiar bond, as Dorothy greeted her with, "O Jellia Jamb! I'm so glad to see you again."

**[[Polychrome]]** — acquaintance. Jellia Jamb seems to have personally attended to Polychrome on her arrival, as she "herself ushered the beautiful Daughter of the Rainbow to her apartments."

page.title: BILLINA
page.content:
## Biography

Billina is a hen who travels in Dorothy's company through the underground realm of the Nome King. Nestled in Dorothy's arms, she draws the attention of the Hungry Tiger, who admits that her "present appearance makes my mouth water" and looks at her "greedily," clicking his jaws, though he ultimately concedes it "wouldn't be right" to eat her. Dorothy addresses her with familiarity, at one point crying, "Why, Billina! Have you been fighting?" When amused, Billina responds not with an ordinary laugh but with "the peculiar cackle that served her for a laugh."

During the search for the Tin Woodman, Billina cackles as she reveals that the little Prince has been carrying him "in his pocket," a claim the Prince immediately denies. She then hushes the child, telling him "the whistle is lost, but you may have another when you get home," showing she is willing to scold even a young royal. The Nome King, for his part, dismisses her contemptuously as a "stupid fowl."

## Biography

Billina is a yellow hen residing in Oz, a fact clarified when the Wizard, unfamiliar with her, asks whether she is a girl and is told otherwise. She is described by Dorothy as a great friend of hers. Billina chose to remain in Oz rather than return to Kansas or travel with Dorothy to Australia, preferring life there. She is mentioned together with other Oz residents, including the Cowardly Lion and his friend the Hungry Tiger, all of whom, according to Dorothy, still live in Oz.

## Biography

Billina is a yellow hen with fluffy feathers and a pearl necklace around her throat, seen perched on the shoulder of the copper man Tik-tok. When Dorothy catches sight of her, she cries out in a glad voice and the hen flies to her arms, where Dorothy hugs and pets her in turn. Dorothy sits down in the road with Billina in her arms and strokes her back while the copper man offers his monotonous welcome to Oz. Billina tells Dorothy she has "some wonderful news" to share with her.

## Relationships

**[[Dorothy]]** — friend. Dorothy calls Billina "one of my dearest friends," who "mustn't be hurt—now or ever," indicating a close bond between them.

**[[Ozma]]** — Billina's tie to Ozma seems to be one of service: she reports being sent, together with Tik-tok, "to wel-come" Dorothy on Ozma's behalf.

**[[Tik-tok]]** — friend. A reference to Tik-tok having saved "my life—and Billina's life, too" suggests a bond of loyalty between them.

**[[Toto]]** — some tension between Billina and Toto is suggested, though no specific incident is described.

## Biography

The Nome King rules a kingdom from an underground palace, where he holds captive the wife and ten children of Evoldo, the former King of Ev, having enslaved them there. By his own account, he transformed the Queen of Ev and her children into articles of ornament and bric-a-brac scattered through his apartments, sparing them physical labor — a fate he describes as an act of kindness rather than cruelty, a characterization contested by those who come seeking their release. He also possesses a magic belt, later handed over to Ozma. Tiktok, addressing the assembled Army of Oz on the eve of the campaign against him, describes the Nome King as "hon-est and good na-tured," though this assessment stands at odds with the very expedition mounted to free his prisoners.

From Dorothy's perspective, the Nome King is said to have challenged Ozma to identify the enchanted members of the royal family among his ornaments within a set number of guesses, on pain of Ozma herself being turned into an ornament should she fail.

## Relationships

**[[DOROTHY]]** — enemy. An exchange accusing him of having been "cheated" suggests hostility between the two.
**[[Ozma]]** — enemy. Ozma's assembling of the Army of Oz toward making him "liberate the prisoners" suggests she regards him as an adversary.
**[[BILLINA]]** — enemy. A declaration of having "saved you from the Nome King, and you are a slave no longer" suggests Billina acted to free a captive from him.
**[[Queen of Ev]]** — enemy. He enslaved her and her ten children and transformed them into ornaments, an act he frames as kindness but which seems to set him against her.
**[[Scarecrow]]** — enemy. Their recurring association suggests the Scarecrow, too, stood opposed to him, though no direct exchange between them is given.

page.content:
## Biography

The Nome King is the former possessor of the Magic Belt, an artifact described as much more powerful than the Silver Shoes. Dorothy once captured this Magic Belt from him, an event she recalls when explaining how Ozma can watch over her through an enchanted picture. The Yellow Hen later recounts having had adventures with the Nome King in the Land of Ev.

page.title: Roquat
page.content:
## Biography

Roquat, also known as King Roquat or the Nome King, rules an underground cavern beyond the Land of Ev. He once held captive members of the Royal Family of Ev, until Ozma marched there with Dorothy and her army and forced him to liberate them. During that encounter the Scarecrow nearly frightened him into fits by throwing one of Billina's eggs at him, and Dorothy captured his Magic Belt, carrying it away to the Land of Oz.

According to the Tin Woodman, Roquat does not have a kind heart and has harbored thoughts of revenge since his defeat, the liberation of his slaves, and the loss of his Magic Belt. He ordered his Nomes to dig a long tunnel beneath the desert so that he might march his forces into the Emerald City. Dorothy recalls that the Scarecrow once conquered the whole of the Nome King's army using some of Billina's eggs.

## Narrative role

Roquat, known also as King Roquat and as the Nome King, is revealed by Nick Chopper to have ordered a tunnel dug beneath the desert so that his forces, joined by the Whimsies, the Growleywogs, and the Phanfasms, might invade Oz — a plan Ozma had already glimpsed in her Magic Picture.

The Scarecrow's secret countermeasure then succeeds: dust scattered in the tunnel leaves the invading host thirsty, and once they drink from the Forbidden Fountain their hostility is forgotten. Roquat resists but is thrown into the Fountain along with his allies, after which Ozma banishes the rest of the invaders home using the Magic Belt.

## Personality

Roquat, aussi appelé King Roquat ou Nome King, se révèle sans bonté : selon les mots du Tin Woodman, « the Nome King has not a kind heart ». Cette dureté se double d'une rancune froide et patiente plutôt que d'un emportement passager — vaincu et privé de sa Ceinture Magique, il nourrit depuis des pensées de vengeance et fait creuser par ses Nomes un long tunnel sous le désert pour marcher sur la Cité d'Émeraude, signe d'une préméditation méthodique.

L'épisode où le Scarecrow faillit le faire sombrer en crise de panique en lui jetant un œuf de Billina suggère aussi une peur vive et disproportionnée face à une menace en apparence anodine, une fragilité qui tranche avec sa réputation de souverain redoutable.

Son propos adressé au General Guph — regretter de ne pas l'avoir nommé général plus tôt — semble indiquer, chez lui, une capacité, rare, à reconnaître une faute envers un subordonné. Son échange avec le Grand Gallipoot (« Don't let us quarrel now, friends ») pourrait de même suggérer une alliance entretenue avec effort plutôt qu'une confiance naturelle envers ses partenaires de guerre.

## Appearance

Roquat is referred to as the old monarch, ruling from his underground cavern beyond the Land of Ev.

## Powers

Roquat's authority as King of the Nomes was bound to a Magic Belt, an artifact of power that Dorothy captured from him and carried away to the Land of Oz.

## Relationships

**[[Ozma]]** — enemy. Their conflict seems to trace back to the time Ozma marched with Dorothy and an army into his underground cavern, beyond the Land of Ev, and forced him to liberate the captives belonging to the Royal Family of Ev.

**[[General Guph]]** — employment. An exchange in which he tells Guph, "I'm sorry I did not make you my General before," suggests Guph serves under him as a general in his forces.

**[[Dorothy]]** — enemy. Their rivalry appears linked to the moment Dorothy captured his Magic Belt and carried it away to the Land of Oz.

**[[Scarecrow]]** — enemy. This antagonism seems to stem from an episode in which the Scarecrow, using one of Billina's eggs, reportedly frightened him into fits, and in which the Scarecrow is said to have once conquered his entire army with Billina's eggs.

**[[Grand Gallipoot]]** — wary alliance. Their association suggests a cautious cooperation, hinted at by an appeal that "friends" not quarrel among themselves.

## Trivia

- Les œufs de Billina semblent constituer une faiblesse particulière chez Roquat : un seul œuf lancé par l'Épouvantail a suffi à le plonger dans des crises de panique, et son armée tout entière aurait déjà été vaincue par plusieurs de ces mêmes œufs.

page.title: Tiktok
page.content:
## Biography

Tiktok is a mechanical man, referred to as "the machine" and "the copper man," who moves only when his machinery has been wound. Invited by Ozma, he takes his seat in the drawing-room of the palace between the Scarecrow and the Tin Woodman, opposite Ozma and Princess Langwidere. When the Tin Woodman describes the army being assembled to face the Nome King, Tiktok asks, "Why should you fight the Nome King?" Asked by Ozma whether he will join the party, Tiktok declares himself "the slave of the girl Dor-oth-y, who res-cued me from pris-on," adding, "Where she goes I will go."

Tiktok is reunited with the Scarecrow and the Tin Woodman after a separation, squeezing the Tin Woodman's hand so earnestly that he dents some of the Tin Woodman's fingers. He is present at the coronation of King Evardo Fifteenth of Ev and, still claiming to belong to Dorothy, is permitted to join the party crossing the desert on Ozma's magic carpet after Dorothy winds his machinery as far as possible.

## Relationships

**[[DOROTHY]]** — Tiktok declares himself "the slave of the girl Dor-oth-y, who res-cued me from pris-on," indicating a bond of loyal service to her that leads him to follow wherever she goes.

**[[Nome King]]** — Tiktok questions the army mustered against the Nome King, asking "Why should you fight the Nome King?," which suggests an adversarial position within the expedition sent to confront him.

**[[Scarecrow]]** — Their shared presence in Ozma's court, seated together with the Tin Woodman, suggests a familiar acquaintance, though no direct exchange between them is recorded.

**[[Ozma]]** — Ozma's direct invitation for Tiktok to join her company, "Will you join our party?," suggests an acquaintance built on her welcome of him into the group.

**[[Tin Woodman]]** — The warmth of their reunion, in which Tiktok squeezes the Tin Woodman's hand "so earnestly that he dented some of his fingers," suggests a close friendship between them.

## Biography

Tik-tok is a copper man. A yellow hen with fluffy feathers and a pearl necklace is perched on his shoulder when Dorothy runs toward him, calling his name. He lifts the little girl in his copper arms and kisses her cheek with his copper lips, greeting her warmly. The hen, later identified as Billina, treats Tik-tok's shoulder as a place of safety — when the dog Toto threatens her, she flies back to perch there, out of reach.

## Relationships

**[[Dorothy]]** — friend. Their bond seems close, as the copper man lifted her in his copper arms and kissed her cheek when she ran to greet him.

**[[Nick Chopper]]** — friend. The copper man and the tin man are said to have been good friends.

**[[Billina]]** — friend. The yellow hen takes refuge on Tik-tok's shoulder when endangered, which could suggest he once saved her life.

**[[Button-Bright]]** — friend. A bond between them is suggested, though no direct exchange is recorded in the excerpts.

**[[Ozma]]** — employment. An association with Ozma is suggested, hinting at some form of service, though its nature is not detailed.

## Biography

Tiktok is a machine man who declares his intent to stand by Ozma, reasoning he "should be of no use at all in Kan-sas." Unlike some of his companions, he has no need to sleep, and is found wandering the palace grounds through the night beside the Tin Woodman and Jack Pumpkinhead until daybreak. He describes his own thinking as mechanical in nature, remarking, "I can on-ly think by ma-chin-er-y, so I do not pre-tend to know as much as you do," a modest assessment offered in response to another's claim of unexcelled wisdom.

## Relationships

**[[Jack Pumpkinhead]]** — their shared company at the palace grounds and the Forbidden Fountain could indicate a friendly acquaintance.

**[[Omby Amby]]** — the connection between them appears only as an indirect acquaintance.

**[[Scarecrow]]** — their shared night by the Forbidden Fountain suggests a friendly bond among the group.

page.title: Prince
page.content:
## Biography

The Prince, whose name is Evring, is a Prince of Ev. Found as a small enchanted purple kitten, he had no memory of his past until Dorothy rescued him and returned him to his true form; once restored, he proudly announced his identity and lineage, though he recalled nothing of what had happened to him after his transformation.

By his own account, his father, the King, sold his mother and all her children to the cruel ruler of the Nomes. His brother Evardo, older than Evring, was among these siblings and stood to inherit their father's throne as King of Ev.

After his rescue, Evring rode with Dorothy upon the Sawhorse, having overcome his early shyness to become fond of the girl who had saved him. The two rode together and talked pleasantly, and Evring marveled, along with Dorothy, at Billina the hen's ability to speak sensibly.

During the journey, Evring came into unwitting possession of the Tin Woodman's enchanted whistle, having pocketed it without meaning to trap its owner. Billina revealed that the whistle, when touched and spoken over with the word "Ev," restored the Tin Woodman instantly. Evring, upon realizing the whistle had been taken from him in turn, cried out for its return.

## Narrative role

Prince Evring is a Prince of Ev, the youngest son of the Queen of Ev, who had been enchanted as a purple kitten after his father the King sold his mother and all her children to the cruel ruler of the Nomes, the Nome King. Dorothy is allowed to guess among the Nome King's ornaments and succeeds in freeing him, restoring Evring to his true form. Once free, Evring rides with Dorothy upon the Sawhorse, having recovered from his early shyness and grown fond of the girl who rescued him; the two become fast friends and converse pleasantly as they travel, and Evring marvels that Billina, a hen, can talk and say such sensible things.

Later, Billina reveals that Evring had accidentally trapped the Tin Woodman by pocketing his enchanted whistle without realizing what it did, and that blowing the whistle while saying Ev restores the Tin Woodman instantly. Evring protests that he only took the whistle, and when Billina reclaims it he begins to cry and asks for it back, prompting Billina to hush him.

## Personality

Evring shows an early pride in his own identity and lineage: recovering his memory, he announces, "I am a Prince of Ev, and my name is Evring," proudly, before recounting his family's fate at the hands of the Nome King. This same proclamation reveals a residual attachment to his lost family, since he can recall nothing beyond his parents' misfortune yet still identifies himself first and foremost as their son.

Though initially shy, he warms quickly to those who help him: once free of enchantment, he becomes very fond of Dorothy, riding beside her and chatting pleasantly, suggesting a trusting and affectionate disposition once his reserve is overcome.

His reaction to the whistle incident reveals a more childlike, defensive streak. Accused by Billina of having trapped the Tin Woodman in his pocket, he protests indignantly, "I did not!", before immediately qualifying his denial with "I only took the whistle" — an instinct to deny wrongdoing paired with an underlying honesty that will not let the correction stand uncorrected. When the whistle is subsequently taken from him, he begins to cry and demands, "I want my whistle!", betraying a childish attachment to small possessions and an emotional volatility consistent with his youth.

## Appearance

Evring is described as a small child, referred to as "the little one" and "the little Prince." Before his true form was restored, he had been transformed into a purple kitten, a shape from which Dorothy rescued him.

## Relationships

**[[DOROTHY]]** — friend. Evring rides with Dorothy upon the Sawhorse and becomes fast friends with her after she rescues him from an enchanted state; Dorothy resolves to save his siblings and, "perhaps," his mother as well.

**[[BILLINA]]** — acquaintance. Evring pockets the Tin Woodman's whistle without realizing its purpose, prompting Billina to reveal the mishap and demonstrate how blowing it restores the Tin Woodman.

**[[Nome King]]** — enemy. Evring recounts that his father the King "sold my mother and all her children to the cruel ruler of the Nomes," casting the Nome King as the one responsible for his family's captivity.

**[[Queen of Ev]]** — family. Evring is one of the Queen's children, and he stands among his siblings "beside their happy mother" once she is restored.

**[[Evardo]]** — family. Evring is named as the younger brother of Evardo, "who was older than his brother Evring."

## Trivia

- Evring once carried the Tin Woodman's enchanted whistle in his pocket without realizing what it was capable of; when Billina touched it and spoke the word "Ev," the Tin Woodman appeared at once, restored from wherever the whistle had held him.
- When the whistle was taken from him so the Tin Woodman could be freed, Evring protested and cried, "I want my whistle!"

## Biography

The Prince presides over the glass city of the Mangaboos, a vegetable people living beneath the earth's crust. His subjects address him as "my Lord," and when wonders appeared in the air, the Prince and all of his people flocked out of the hall into the street to see them. He listens with attention to those who address him, as when he remarked on a visitor "from the crust of the earth" who had called a companion a Wizard.

## Relationships

**[[WIZARD]]** — acquaintance. The Prince addressed the Wizard directly and listened attentively to him, suggesting an acquaintance between the two.

**[[DOROTHY]]** — acquaintance. Cooccurrence in the same scenes suggests some acquaintance with Dorothy, though the excerpts do not detail the nature of this bond.

**[[Princess]]** — other. Cooccurrence suggests a connection with the Princess, though its nature is unclear from the available excerpts.

**[[Sorcerer]]** — employment. Cooccurrence during the Sorcerer's display of sorcery in the Prince's hall could indicate the Sorcerer serves under the Prince's authority.

**[[Zeb]]** — enemy. Cooccurrence suggests some tension with Zeb, though the excerpts do not clarify the nature of this bond.

page.title: Evardo
page.content:
## Biography

Evardo is a prince of Ev, one of four princes and five princesses born to the Queen of Ev, all of whom resemble one another closely except in size. He is older than his brother Evring. As the eldest of the royal children, Evardo stood to inherit his father's throne and be crowned King of Ev upon returning to his own country; he is described as a grave and quiet youth who would rule his people wisely and with justice.

After the Queen was relieved of her enchanted duties, she presented Evardo to the assembled subjects from a palace balcony as their future ruler, proclaiming him "King Evardo Fifteenth" — fifteen years of age, wearing fifteen silver buckles on his jacket, and the fifteenth Evardo to rule the land of Ev. The people cheered their approval fifteen times, and even the Wheelers present pledged their obedience to the new King. The Queen then set a crown of gold, adorned with rubies, upon his head and draped an ermine robe over his shoulders, formally proclaiming him King. Evardo bowed gratefully to his subjects before going off to look for cake in the royal pantry.

## Relationships

**[[Queen of Ev]]** — family. He stood in a row beside his mother among her restored children, one of her nine sons and daughters.

**[[Prince]]** — family. He was older than his brother Evring, suggesting a fraternal bond between the two princes of Ev.
